<!-- p. 103 -->

The *mestre* had not intended to take an apprentice so soon, but the magical powers he sensed in Ágata were so strong that, although their specialties were completely different, Sesnando finally agreed. Besides, the girl was already of an age, and it would soon be too late to train her properly. Ágata was eleven when she joined the covenant, and she has spent the last six years trying to control her magical arts with uneven success, to the frustration of both herself and her master. Although Sesnando has managed to instill in her the rudiments of Bonisagus's magic theory and to channel her potential within Hermetic teaching (at least as the *rusticani* apply it), Ágata has such a whirlwind of magical energy within her that even the simplest effects often slip out of her control. The nine years of apprenticeship she has left will no doubt prove difficult.

What is clear is that Ágata has a potential that many Hermetic magi consider wasted. Any visiting magus would regard her as a rough jewel waiting to be cut, with a brilliant future if she were in the right environment and had a worthy mentor. One such magus is Mauricio, the Verditius of Porta Pandere (see below), who, having met Ágata on a visit to the range two years ago and discovered that her gifts could be very valuable to the members of his House, has returned to the covenant a couple more times intending to persuade Sesnando to give up Ágata as his *filia*. Faced with Sesnando's refusal, Mauricio is considering turning to some Guernicus to look for an irregularity in her apprenticeship that would let him take Ágata away from him. He would not even rule out negotiating with some Bonisagus to take her as an apprentice, exploiting that House's privileges.

> #### The Magic of the Rusticani
>
> The *rusticani* tradition bases its magic on the Major Virtue Craft Magic, which has four main applications, almost always tied to a Craft Ability (in Ágata's case, Stonemason): first, the *rusticani* can dispense with gestures and words when casting magic; instead they use an object they have carved themselves, into which the effect in question has been invested. When making this preparation, they receive a shape and material bonus for the object, limited by their score in the Craft. They can also create charged items in less time than usual (they take as long as it would take to make the mundane object, multiplied by the number of copies they make, with a Lab Total equal to their Casting Total), and, finally, they can turn objects containing raw vis into lesser enchanted devices, following parameters similar to those for charged items (although it is enough to exceed the level of the effect, rather than double it, to complete the item in a single season).
>
> The Minor Virtue Spell Foci allows the *rusticani* to have small tools that help them cast magic, adding a shape and material bonus, again limited by their Magic Theory or their Craft. They make heavy use of these *foci* when casting spontaneous magic, since their innate abilities, closely bound up with the magical capacities of objects, limit their natural spontaneous magic and oblige them to take the Major Hermetic Flaw Weak Spontaneous Magic, under which they cannot expend Fatigue when casting spontaneous magic, so all their Casting Totals must be divided by five and do not add a die roll.
>
> #### Story Seeds: Princess Peralta
>
> Legend has it that the castle of Lousã, which stands not far from the covenant, was built by a Muslim king named Arouce, or Arunce, who withdrew there with his daughter, Princess Peralta, when the Christian forces conquered the region. During their hasty flight, the princess's eyes met those of one of the Christian princes, Lausus, and the two fell hopelessly in love. Lausus searched for the princess throughout the range, not knowing that Arouce had locked her up at the very top of the castle, along with all his riches, so that their love would never come to be. Then, determined to do away with his enemy, Arouce waylaid him as he traveled through the range, and a terrible duel ensued that ended both their lives. Since only the king knew that Peralta was locked away, it is said that the princess died in there, with no one able to save her. Ever since, on certain nights of the year, wails and screams are heard at the top of the castle, which many attribute to the tormented soul of Princess Peralta.
>
> When the castle was occupied by Christian forces in the second half of the twelfth century, the legend came back to life, and many speak of screams and noises of no clear origin. In truth, Peralta's spirit still dwells in a small *regio* formed at the top of the castle tower, surrounded by the same treasures with which her father locked her away. What will the magi of Serra da Lousã do when one of the local peasants claims to have seen the princess herself begging to be freed from her eternal torment?

<!-- p. 104 -->

As for Ágata, beyond the problems with her magic, she is very happy under Sesnando's tutelage. Just as the *mestre* did in his youth, he lets the girl visit her parents whenever she wishes, and they are more than content to see their daughter a couple of times a month and confirm that she is well. Ágata also has a curious relationship with Facundo, whom she admires both for his skill as a craftsman and for his deep convictions. Unlike the old man, the girl can tell the difference between belief and magic, but she thinks it is precisely the *velho*'s piety that gives his items their special touch, and she would like to have that same ability when investing magic in her creations.

### Inverneira

>**Lifespan:** 857–907<br>
>**Founder:** Isidoro of Bonisagus<br>
>**Aura (type and strength):** Magic, strength 3<br>
>**Reputations:** Scholars (Iberian Tribunal) 3

During its few years of life, the short-lived covenant of Inverneira was a beacon of learning in the northwest of the Peninsula. Unfortunately, the end of the truce with the *saḥirs* prevented great discoveries that might have benefited the whole Order of Hermes from being made there.

#### History

In the early days of the Peninsula, Baldiccione dreamed of a Tribunal that would rival the Rhine itself as a cradle of learning. He knew that this would require a Durenmar, a place devoted solely to the gathering and transmission of knowledge. And so, when he met Isidoro, a Bonisagus from the Rhine who was obsessed with collecting knowledge, he saw his chance. Thanks to the peace with the *saḥirs*, he was able to establish a covenant devoted to research, and together with Isidoro he soon found the ideal place for it: an islet in the middle of one of the so-called Seven Lakes of Peneda, in natural surroundings of majestic beauty.

Isidoro named his covenant Inverneira, from the Galician-Portuguese for "winter," for he saw it as a refuge in which any knowledge in danger of disappearing in the outside world could be sheltered. The Bonisagus set to work immediately after announcing the birth of Inverneira in 857, pouring his knowledge into volumes freely available for study to all the magi of the Order. Many of those volumes were copied, and those copies still survive in many of the covenants of the Peninsula.

But Isidoro's dreams were not limited to copying and transmitting conventional knowledge. He also longed to carry out studies that would reach another level, testing the limits of magic. Thus the Isidorian Circle was born. Unfortunately, he was never able to make his dream come true: in 907, after more than forty years of silence, the *saḥirs* launched an attack on the north of the Peninsula that swept away several covenants, Inverneira among them. The *saḥirs*' jinn had no trouble crossing the waters that served as the covenant's main protection and razing the magi's dwelling.

#### Setting and Physical Description

Inverneira rose on a small islet in the middle of one of the many lakes in the Peneda area, a few hours' journey from the city of Braga. The region is remarkable for its imposing natural landscapes, dotted with lakes, waterfalls and ravines, into which scarcely any road penetrates. This wild character was Inverneira's main defense, as was its location, for the covenant could only be reached by water, in some boat that crossed the stretch separating the shores of the lake from the small islet.

> #### Story Seeds: The Isidorian Circle
>
> Inverneira soon became more than a repository of knowledge, and its magi more than mere copyists distributing that knowledge throughout the Order. With Isidoro as director of research, the covenant became the nerve center of a great project, that of the Isidorian Circle, on which many other magi of the Tribunal worked, most of them Bonisagi. The role of the Redcaps of Aedes Saturni in keeping communication flowing among all the project's participants was key, and the progress of their work was so brilliant that the Redcaps were soon being employed by the rest of the Tribunal's members, who began to stop regarding them as a dead weight on the Order.
>
> The *saḥir* attack of 907 cut that enormous project short at a stroke. It is said that the Circle was making good progress on its main subject of study, which was none other than breaking the limit of Arcane Connections; had it been completed, it would have allowed Hermetic magi to affect an unseen target without having an Arcane Connection to it. Isidoro had spoken to those close to him about the possibility of breaking that limit by creating new Range parameters, but unfortunately no one today knows how far they progressed in that study. Nor is it known how far they progressed in another of their secondary projects (far less well known, for obvious reasons), which consisted of integrating the magic of the tempestarii, who only a few decades earlier had caused the Order so much trouble.
>
> Almost 300 years have passed since the fall of Inverneira, but no one has dared to venture into its ruins. Perhaps the player magi would like to make a foray to the old islet in search of some remnant of the research the Circle carried out over fifty years.

<!-- p. 105 -->

The covenant consisted of a small, square, Romanesque building that was almost reminiscent of a monastery, surrounded by a few outbuildings for the mundane population. The magi of Inverneira always lived in relative austerity, which meant that the few travelers who passed nearby sometimes took them for a religious community. Unfortunately, since the attack of the *saḥirs* more than three centuries ago, very few have ventured into the wind-lashed ruins of the building, which are the only remains of the community that once lived here.

Inverneira had within its reach numerous rich vis sources scattered across what will become the province of *Trás-os-Montes*, which have survived unchanged thanks to the isolation and sparse population of the region. Although almost all those sources are currently being exploited by the covenants of Porta Pandere and Duresca, this region would be an ideal place for the creation of a Spring covenant of an isolationist bent.

### Langobriga

>**Lifespan:** 1075–1139<br>
>**Founders:** Gonçalo "the Giant" of Flambeau; Proditor of Tremere<br>
>**Aura (type and strength):** Magic, strength 4<br>
>**Reputations:** Rebels (Iberian Tribunal) 3

Expelled from the covenant of Duresca because of their bitter disagreements with its inner council, the magi who founded Langobriga revived the ancient myth of Castro de Ovil, according to which the site was the ancient capital of the *Turduli Veteres*, or "Old Turduli," an ancient Iberian people who lived in Roman times. Langobriga had a fleeting existence, which came to an end after its part in the battle of Ourique, where both founders lost their lives.

#### History

In 1076 Gonçalo the Giant, a Flambeau magus of enormous size who had completed his apprenticeship at Duresca, decided to leave what had been his home for the past several years, weary of what he regarded as the oppression and tyranny of the ruling elite of the Order of Hermes. Accompanied by Proditor of Tremere, another disgruntled magus who lived in the same covenant, the two traveled south in search of a place where they could settle and be truly free. On reaching the region of Espinho, they heard stories about the so-called *Turduli Veteres*, an ancient Iberian people of Roman times who had fought fiercely to preserve their independence. Seduced by the myth, Gonçalo and Proditor settled in an old hillfort that had been abandoned for centuries and raised their covenant there, naming it Langobriga in honor of the ancient capital of the Turduli.

Once freed from the "Hermetic yoke," Gonçalo and Proditor threw themselves into feverish activity, rebuilding the hillfort, furnishing it with a few additional comforts and taking an active part in both the mundane and Hermetic politics of the region, fully exercising their "freedom." This consisted essentially of fishing in the troubled waters of the Tribunal at that time, in the midst of the schism between Iberia and al-Andalus, making constant raids to the south while becoming a thorn in the side of some powerful covenants in the north. Their part in the famous Tribunal of 1081 was notorious: they tried by every means to prevent the ultimatum to al-Andalus with fiery proclamations of liberty. Unfortunately, they did not yet have enough political influence for their involvement to change the decision.

The zeal and fervor of the magi of Langobriga led them to take part in the battle of Ourique in 1139. The magi had joined Alfonso's host, drawn by the magical riches they might recover by fighting in the south, and they offered their powers in the service of the future Portuguese king. Unfortunately, Gonçalo and Proditor fell in battle, which ultimately meant the end of the covenant when Gonçalo's only apprentice, Baltasar, was adopted by a Bonisagus of Duresca, since he had not yet completed his apprenticeship when the battle took place. The hillfort was abandoned and, since Baltasar was not yet a magus in his own right, most of its riches and possessions passed to Duresca: what seemed a cruel joke of fate.

> #### Story Seeds: In hoc signo vinces
>
> What were the magi of Langobriga doing so far from home when they fell at the battle of Ourique? The answer to that question died with them, but some descendants of those who lived at the covenant in the 1130s might know the reason for the journey: in truth, Gonçalo and Proditor had discovered the existence of a powerful vis source through certain ancient texts that had come into their possession. The source lay in Almoravid territory, very close to the southern coast of the Peninsula. Such a foray was too bold to undertake alone, so they offered their help to the then Count Alfonso when they learned that he was about to launch a raid to the south, in exchange for his promise to help them in their purpose when the time came.
>
> Unfortunately, fortune did not smile on the magi of Langobriga. While they were falling in battle, legend says, Alfonso heard the voice of God at Ourique. It said to him: *in hoc signo vinces* ("in this sign you shall conquer"), referring to the symbol of the cross, which would be incorporated into the arms of Portugal together with the symbols of the five Muslim kings defeated in that battle.
>
> If someone were to speak with one of those descendants, or investigate the ruins of Langobriga, they might find more information about that vis source. The Peninsula has changed a great deal since then, and perhaps a journey to claim it would be more feasible today…

<!-- p. 106 -->

#### Setting and Physical Description

Langobriga stood on a hill bounded to the south and west by the banks of the Paramos river, which framed a promontory covered with dense woodland. The sea lay less than five kilometers to the west, and barely a hundred meters away ran the main Roman road linking Lisbon with the city of Braga. The covenant had the same layout as the ancient hillforts and lay within an oval wall at the top of the hill; inside, past a ditch, were two terraces: one with various huts and small structures where the mundane community lived, and an upper enclosure, or "croa," where the magi lived, in an eminently military setting. They had scarcely any space set aside for a library, and each magus kept his personal treasure in his own *sanctum*.

The hillfort was abandoned shortly after the battle of Ourique, and rumors about the strange powers of its occupants have kept anyone from daring to venture in and explore it. Its half-ruined structures remain completely uninhabited to this day.

## The Southern Region

With a much milder climate than the north, the southern region's relief grows gentler toward the south, where, past the Tagus river, there are more cork oaks, a tree the Portuguese exploit for its cork and acorns, as well as plantations of great olive groves. In general, in this region deciduous trees gradually give way to evergreens.

Here lie the prominent city of Lisbon and the renowned town of Santarém. The cities of Évora and Alcácer do Sal border the Almohad province of al-Andalus to the south and east; the region's other frontiers are the Atlantic Ocean to the west and the kingdom of Leon to the east.

With the advance of the Portuguese frontier, Hermetic magi have gradually settled the northern territories of Portugal, which in 1220 have two living covenants: the powerful Mercer House of Porta Pandere and the promising Resurgens.

### Porta Pandere

>**Lifespan:** 990–Present<br>
>**Founders:** Parcus of Mercere; Jadiya ḅint Talib al-Gernikiyya<br>
>**Season:** Autumn<br>
>**Aura (type and strength):** Magic, strength 4<br>
>**Reputations:** Opulent (Iberian Tribunal) 3; Treacherous (Iberian Flambeau) 2<br>
>**Votes:** 5

Born as the second Mercer House of the Tribunal, Porta Pandere has been characterized throughout its history by its abundant material wealth and by holding a highly unorthodox position on certain questions of Hermetic politics, unlike Aedes Saturni, with which it has a fierce rivalry.

#### History

At the end of the tenth century the Order of Hermes, and more specifically House Mercere, was in full expansion across North Africa. Taking advantage of a legal loophole in the undertaking given to the *saḥirs* not to found covenants on that continent, the Redcaps established the Mercer House of Aedes Iris; located in the oasis of Tāfīlālt, it gathered a good part of the wealth that the Redcaps channeled northward from the surrounding lands.

A side effect of the creation of Aedes Iris was the approval for the creation, now in the Peninsula, of another Mercer House that would serve as a second great communication hub in Iberia. Whereas Aedes Saturni, in Barcelona, had portals linking the covenant with Iberia and with other points such as distant Harco, the new covenant would have new portals that would not only reinforce that network within the Peninsula but would also link to Aedes Iris.

The task of founding this new covenant fell to two magi, Parcus of Mercere and Jadiya ḅint Talib al-Gernikiyya. The former had completed his apprenticeship at Aedes Saturni, where he had lived for some years before leaving the covenant, dissatisfied with its internal and external policies. Jadiya, for her part, was a native of Cáceres and had studied at Dār Malīḥaʾ under the aegis of Zaynab (see Chapter IX). Unlike Parcus, Jadiya always maintained cordial relations with her home covenant.

The site the two magi chose for the covenant was a small range of hills not far from the city of Santarém, where, according to the ancient legends of the region, Abidis, ancestral king of the Lusitanians, had lived. The name they chose for the new covenant was Porta Pandere, in honor of the goddess Empanda, an epithet of the Roman Juno in her aspect as goddess of hospitality and charity. Porta Pandere was thus born as a place of refuge for those in need of protection, subsidiary to the principal Mercer House of Iberia, Aedes Saturni. The paranoia of the Catalan Mercere, however, had led them to view the Order's expansion into Africa with suspicion and to refuse any direct communication with that region by means of portals. The fact that Porta Pandere did have direct contact with Africa would clearly shape their relationship from the beginning, as would its ambivalent commitment to the pro-Andalusi movement that would cause the Hermetic schism in Iberia.

<!-- p. 107 -->

After its founding, Porta Pandere began to make use of the volume of wealth arriving from Africa to increase its autonomy from Aedes Saturni and establish itself as a powerful covenant. It also supported the group of covenants that decided to break away from the north of Iberia to form an independent Tribunal. The combined economic power of Aedes Iris and Porta Pandere would in fact be one of the main driving forces of the new Tribunal. Thus, in 1012, at the first Tribunal of al-Andalus, the covenant was chosen as the seat of the Andalusi treasury, the equivalent of the funds held by the magi of the north. As at Aedes Saturni, the treasury would be guarded by two magi, holding the offices of *ḥárisun* and *jāzin*. That same year the so-called "Iberian tax" was abolished in the covenants of the Tribunal of al-Andalus, and it was decided to set up a mint at Porta Pandere to strike coin, taking advantage of the abundant flow of metal arriving from *bilad al-Sūdān*. Fundamental to all these maneuvers was the presence of Parcus, who in those years earned the nickname Parcus Pecunius for his relentless commercial mentality and his ingenuity in orchestrating Porta Pandere's economic hegemony over the whole south of Iberia. The loss of that economic power was also a hard blow for the magi of the north, and many accused the Mercere of treachery at a time when the whole Order was convulsed by the effects of the Schism War.

It was also Parcus who sent a group of Redcaps to the auction of the riches of Madīnat al-Zahrāʾ and Madīnat al-Zaḥirāʾ organized by the governor of Cordoba. There they acquired all kinds of luxurious objects that in many cases would decorate the halls of Porta Pandere, as well as not a few volumes that had escaped Almanzor's burning and that expanded the covenant's mundane library. Other acquisitions went to the Great Hall in Saragossa, of which Porta Pandere was always one of the main supporters. By then the prosperity and wealth of Porta Pandere had led its magi to question the point of their subordination to Aedes Saturni. With Jadiya's help, Parcus began a correspondence with Harco to obtain independence from the Mercer House in Barcelona, beginning a complex legal battle in which their membership of an independent Tribunal, although it was never officially recognized by the Order of Hermes, was a weighty argument. In 1038, at last, Porta Pandere obtained full autonomy from Aedes Saturni. It was also around then that the Mercere accepted the proposal to open a new portal, *Vicesimus*, linking directly with the covenant of Dār Malīḥaʾ.

In the following decades Porta Pandere continued to prosper, always drawing on the flow of wealth coming from Aedes Iris. More than once the covenant had to send several Redcaps backed by men-at-arms to defend the African Mercer House in regional conflicts, but the most important change was Jadiya's gradual decline. The covenant's co-founder had always been one of the chief instigators of the creation of the Tribunal of al-Andalus, and when she succumbed to Final Twilight in 1075, something changed forever in the covenant. Parcus, by then an aged magus showing certain signs of senility, ordered a complete reversal of the covenant's foreign policy. Many today believe that his support for Jadiya over the decades was merely a pretext for gaining autonomy from Aedes Saturni and becoming a powerful Mercer House in its own right. Now that Jadiya was gone, he could take off the mask and take the next step in his plan.

That step came in 1082, when the foundations of the fledgling Tribunal began to crack. When the Guernicus of the new Tribunal, fearful of a repeat of the Schism War, suggested dissolving al-Andalus, Porta Pandere announced that it would not support the magi of the south if they insisted on their independence. The decision surprised friend and foe alike, and many sent emissaries to the covenant to make them change their minds. But Parcus had made his decision, and at the Tribunal of 1089 it was ratified. That decision was, together with the skillful intervention of the diplomats from the north, a key factor in the dissolution of the Tribunal of al-Andalus and the reunification of all the covenants of Iberia. Paradoxically, Aedes Iris maintained its support for independence, which led to a deterioration in relations between the two covenants. Although wealth from Africa would continue to arrive through the *Tertius Decimus* portal, the terms of trade grew steadily harsher. Porta Pandere's dazzling prosperity slowed in the following years as the dream of al-Andalus faded away for good. That slowdown became even more evident with the reunification of Iberia and the clause of 1116 under which the Tribunal's treasuries would be divided between Aedes Saturni and Porta Pandere, partly rekindling the rivalry between the two Mercer Houses that had been born half a century earlier.

That prosperity was cut short for good by the inexplicable destruction of Aedes Iris on a fateful night in 1123. To this day no one knows what caused the disappearance of the Mercer House in Africa, but its consequences were immediate and devastating for Porta Pandere: without the metal arriving from Africa the mint no longer made sense, so the covenant closed its *dār al-sikka* at once. In that same decade the covenant also lost Parcus, when the Mercere was more than a century and a half old. His successor, son and apprentice, Paulo, lacked the gifts and ambition of his *parens* and was utterly overwhelmed by the turbulent situation of those years. Unfortunately for him, but fortunately for the covenant, another of Parcus's apprentices (and also his son), the young Alexander, decided to intervene, and over the years won the support of the covenant's other magi until in 1165 he managed to oust his own brother and take his place as *princeps* of the covenant (the year in which it obtained the title of dedicated covenant for the Hermetic Inn of Occelum Durii; see page 142). Alexander changed his name to Parcus Minor, revived his master's philosophy and embarked on an aggressive economic policy, using his Redcaps as pawns to establish a subtle network of control over information and wealth in the region.

<!-- p. 108 -->

Over the last century, Porta Pandere has tried to regain its hegemony in southern Iberia under the iron control of Parcus Minor. More than once it has tried to establish new Mercer Houses in Africa to recover its lost economic glory, without success so far. In 1220 it is negotiating with the covenant of al-Minẓār, but Gonçalvo has proved an insurmountable rival even for Parcus Minor's considerable diplomatic gifts. Now, with the year 1225 approaching, when the Order will at last be able to establish itself in Africa, Parcus is waiting on events, ready to grant the concession for the unopened portal at Porta Pandere to any covenant willing to send new riches to the Peninsula.

#### Setting and Physical Description

Porta Pandere lies in the Sierra de Montejunto, a small range of hills a day's journey west of the city of Santarém. In ancient times the legendary king of the Lusitanians known as Abidis, or Habidis, lived there. The site chosen was a flat area on the lower slopes of the range, where the magi found a faint latent magic aura, probably the result of some battle fought by that king in antiquity. They soon raised a small fortification there, around which a few minor structures and small farms were added, until it became a self-sufficient community that lived off the crops of the surrounding lands and began to receive the flow of African riches through its portal. That wealth allowed the magi of Porta Pandere to expand and strengthen the main stronghold, as well as to provide the community with all manner of advances and improvements so that it could maintain its self-sufficiency.

Today the covenant is divided into two clearly distinct parts: the main stronghold and the farms and fields that surround it. The stronghold, where the magi live, is a square fort with thick walls of pale stone and a sober appearance, deliberately so, to discourage attacks on such an isolated place. But once one crosses the drawbridge and enters, the picture changes radically. The main courtyard is adorned with delicate statues and surrounded by a colonnaded gallery floored with white marble, and the inner walls are hung with standards, tapestries and pennants. The doorways to the chambers are dressed with curtains of fine silk, and throughout the interior of the fortification one can see a delicate yet luxurious mixture of styles that betrays Porta Pandere's privileged status.

The inner chambers of the fortification include the magi's *sancta* (as well as a few empty ones for visitors), the library (with a well-stocked mundane section that not only rivals but surpasses that of Aedes Saturni) and the treasury, where precious metals and stones of incalculable value brought from Africa are kept. The covenant's vis stores are also abundant, although their volume has begun to shrink drastically since the destruction of Aedes Iris.

Nevertheless, the most striking structure at Porta Pandere is without doubt the hall of portals, set in a single underground chamber more than twenty meters across. Tiled and paneled in fine white marble decorated with gold and precious stones, the chamber is the greatest display of the wealth Porta Pandere once enjoyed. Its center is dominated by an enormous round table of wrought iron damascened with gold and silver, at which the Redcaps who guard the hall and control the comings and goings through the portals usually sit. The table is enchanted with various Hermetic effects that allow the Redcaps to control the opening and closing of the portals, as well as some other defensive effect. Around the entire perimeter of the hall the outlines of six doors are carved, each decorated with different metals and gems and bearing a different name on its lintel: *Decimus* (opals), *Undecimus* (silver), *Duodecimus* (sapphires), *Tertius Decimus* (gold, although this has been removed from the carving since the portal was annulled) and *Vicesimus* (topazes). The sixth door has neither name nor decoration, since the Mercere carved it only in case they needed to open another portal in the future.

Outside the stronghold lives Porta Pandere's mundane community. This includes the Redcaps, eight in all, but also their families, who look after the upkeep of the community, farming the land, selling their produce and also benefiting from the covenant's high standard of living. The dwellings of these people are no hovels or ramshackle huts: they live in solidly built houses of wood or stone, with every comfort imaginable in a rural setting. And although the Redcaps spend more time traveling or in the stronghold than with their own families, their quarters in those houses have little to envy those of certain minor nobles.

#### Society and Customs

Porta Pandere is governed by a strict democracy in which each magus has one vote. The vote of the covenant's leader, always a Mercere magus, counts double in the event of a tie, but that is his only privilege. Although there is no written rule on the matter, the number of magi in the covenant is always kept below five, to prevent as far as possible this democracy from costing House Mercere the iron control it holds over the covenant. What is written is that all Mercere magi living at Porta Pandere must train their apprentices here, and that all those apprentices must spend at least their first seven years as magi in the covenant, in an effort to preserve Parcus's lineage and Mercere hegemony in the covenant.

There is also a lineage of Guernicus magi at Porta Pandere, descended from Jadiya, who almost always come from the south of the Peninsula and are trained at the covenant itself. Traditionally, these Guernicus have always supported the Mercere of Porta Pandere in their dealings, forming a solid alliance that has clearly contributed to the place's past and present prosperity.

Finally, the titles of *ḥárisun* and *jāzin* are still kept, even though Porta Pandere is no longer the sole repository of the Iberian treasury. However, the magi who hold these offices are not usually members of the covenant and therefore have no rights as such, neither voice nor vote. They limit themselves to fulfilling their role as protectors and watchmen, and although the covenant offers them certain advantages for the role they play, very few of them remain at Porta Pandere any longer than necessary once their term ends.

The Redcaps of the mundane community are for the most part more or less distant relatives of Parcus Pecunius's line who have not inherited his Gift. The family line has spread over the generations, sometimes mixing with natives of the region, until it has become a close-knit, peaceful community that takes advantage of Porta Pandere's material privileges to lead a very comfortable life.

<!-- p. 109 -->

#### The Magi of Porta Pandere

Besides its five magi, Porta Pandere has eight Redcaps who travel throughout the south and west of the Peninsula. Foremost among them is Bahir, a direct descendant of Salah, the Redcap who in the eleventh century gathered the African travels of Umm al-Kirām al-Merkeriyya (see Chapter III), which would lead to the founding of Aedes Iris, into a popular *risāla* that many Redcaps still read often today. Bahir, nicknamed "the Red" for his red hair, is a highly talented troubadour who sings that *risāla* (and dramatized versions of some of his own travels) wherever he goes. His great dream is to travel to Africa and emulate the adventures of Umm al-Kirām.

##### Parcus Minor of Mercere

As he approaches his hundredth year, Parcus Minor grows more and more like the founder whose name he bears, who was also his natural and Hermetic father. His innate ambition and genius came to light in the middle of the last century, when, upon Parcus's death, he decided to supplant the legitimate heir to the leadership of the covenant, his brother Paulo. He won the favor and the votes of every magus in the covenant, and since then he has occupied the seat of *princeps* with an iron hand and relentless efficiency. It is thanks to him alone that Porta Pandere has managed to weather the blow dealt by the destruction of Aedes Iris and maintain its privileged status in the south of the Peninsula. Parcus responded to the loss by managing the covenant's wealth with surgical precision, avoiding needless expense and making investments that have almost always proved successful. His acumen and commercial skill have also shone in his Hermetic negotiations, securing favorable agreements with several covenants in Iberia. Only one thorn remains lodged in his side: his rivalry with Aedes Saturni, which still enjoys a greater reputation than Porta Pandere even though the latter probably surpasses it in many respects.

Parcus is an expert in Mentem, and he does not hesitate to use his magic subtly to gain advantage in his dealings, even if that means committing minor violations of the Code of Hermes. He is far too clever to put a foot wrong and does so only when he knows he will not be caught and there are no witnesses, but even so, Dúnya suspects that there is something shady about his dealings.

##### Paulo of Mercere

Paulo is the opposite of his younger brother. As limited as a magus as he is as a negotiator and diplomat, Parcus's firstborn took the loss of his position as *princeps* very badly and, although he still lives in the covenant, he has almost entirely given up playing any active part in its daily life. He has even set aside his Hermetic studies, so that, despite being six years older than Parcus Minor, his development as a magus lags far behind. Now an old man kept alive only by his Longevity Ritual, he has spent several years sunk in wasteful hedonism. Thus Paulo passes his time drinking, eating, consuming white poppy (see page 134) and enjoying the pleasures of the flesh.

<!-- p. 110 -->

Paulo has an innate affinity for Imaginem magic, and it is practically the only Art he has developed in recent decades, to the point of obsession. His laboratory is a fine example of this: a place teeming with illusions almost as perfect as reality itself, but which at the same time reveal Paulo's empty pretensions. Serving girls like houris able to play heavenly music, perfumes so intense they make the head spin, and images of distant, exotic places floating in the air like ethereal mirrors turn the *sanctum* into an extraordinary place.

##### Dúnya Ḅint Kamal al-Gernikiyya

Dúnya belongs to the lineage of Guernicus magi that has always existed at Porta Pandere and that descends from the foundress herself, Jadiya. The covenant's Guernicus have always been reliable allies of the Mercere, and both groups have worked in unison to make Porta Pandere one of the richest and most powerful covenants in the region. Dúnya's own *parens*, Kamal, was extremely accommodating of Parcus Minor's policies throughout the second half of the twelfth century, ignoring many maneuvers that breached the Code of Hermes but clearly benefited Porta Pandere. Dúnya, however, has a much stronger character: not only does she place the Order's law above her covenant's prosperity, but she has also not forgotten what she regards as Parcus's betrayal of Jadiya more than a century ago. That betrayal is more alive than ever today in light of the delicate situation Porta Pandere is going through. And although the Tribunal of al-Andalus is no more than a golden memory for many, she is not prepared to let Parcus Minor repeat his father's abuses and betrayals, and she tries to keep a very close watch on his maneuvers. This makes relations between the two rather tense.

To the outside world, however, Dúnya is a fierce defender of Porta Pandere and usually plays a very active role at Tribunals, championing its interests. This has led to several clashes not only with the Mercere of Aedes Saturni but also with several of the most influential covenants of the north, Duresca included. Many regard her as a potential dissident threat, and some are considering pulling strings to have Magvillus itself assign Dúnya a new post outside Iberia. The maneuver will probably prove unnecessary: Dúnya herself might decide on a change of scene if she cannot curb Parcus's appetites, perhaps traveling to North Africa from the year 1225 onward to establish a covenant there, since she knows full well that the presence of Hermetic law will be needed in those lands yet to be colonized.

##### Atanasio of Flambeau

Atanasio arrived at Porta Pandere in the middle of the twelfth century, when the covenant had not yet fully recovered from the blow of losing Aedes Iris. He was then a young magus sent from Salionca. The Flambeau volunteered to take the post of *ḥárisun* and guard the part of the Hermetic treasury kept at Porta Pandere. During the seven years he held that office he was considered just another *peregrinator*, with no say in the covenant's decisions. In 1168, however, once his term had ended, the newly elevated Parcus Minor decided to offer him a place as a permanent magus of the covenant, convinced that his presence would serve his long-term plans. Atanasio accepted, seduced by Porta Pandere's opulence, and he has since been one of Parcus Minor's most loyal supporters. Today he is not only Parcus's right hand but also the covenant's chief defender should it come under any attack, for although he is close to a hundred years old, he remains in superb shape thanks to a potent Longevity Ritual provided by his former companions at Salionca.

Atanasio has also taken charge of improving the defenses of Porta Pandere's main stronghold, both mundane and magical. Although his enchantments tend to be as devastating as they are showy, Parcus Minor has decided to keep them active in case the covenant should suffer some unexpected attack. Dúnya does not share his view, and fears that any incident could needlessly attract the attention of mundanes.

##### Mauricio of Verditius

Mauricio is the youngest member of the covenant. He arrived at Porta Pandere shortly before the last turn of the century, drawn by tales of the covenant's wealth and of the great number of art objects to be found there. In truth, his intention was to determine whether, among all those treasures, many of them obtained at the Cordoba auction in the eleventh century, there lay one of the lost devices that never turned up at the sale of objects (see Chapter III): the caliph's ring, a prodigious object credited with great powers that never went to auction because it had been concealed within some mundane object (many tales speak of a statue). Although he has no direct connection with either Ajabeba or al-Zahrāʾ, the tale of the caliph's ring reached Mauricio's ears during his training at Verdi, and once he had passed his Gauntlet he decided to travel to Porta Pandere to discover whether the ring was there. Parcus was quick to grasp the worth of the young and skillful magus and accepted his request.

<!-- p. 111 -->

Since his arrival at the covenant, Mauricio has been trying to determine whether the ring is hidden in any of Porta Pandere's statues or other objects. So far he has not succeeded, but he has not given up, although he pursues the quest with ever less zeal, since he has found a better use for his Hermetic time: enchanting some of those same art objects with effects that may be useful to the covenant. His brilliance and finesse are not yet on a par with the masters of al-Zahrāʾ, but he certainly enjoys a privileged opportunity to work with materials of the finest quality.

> #### Story Seeds: Beyond the Ring of Fire
>
> Parcus Minor has very specific plans for the blind portal in Porta Pandere's hall of portals. Although he has received offers from various covenants and factions in Iberia, Parcus harbors ambitious dreams in which he imagines himself restoring the covenant's former riches, surpassing even the heights reached by his father and predecessor. To that end, he has begun to hatch a plan to exploit the riches he knows must exist beyond *bilad al-Sūdān*, further east than the Order of Hermes has ever reached in Africa and further south than the lands of the Egyptians and the Nubians. In 1225 the Order will be able to establish new settlements in Africa, and so he is preparing an expedition of Redcaps and magi to cross the great desert and establish a permanent covenant in those lands, perhaps even beyond Ethiopia.
>
> Parcus knows that his ambitious plan must not reach indiscreet ears, and so he is secretly sounding out some young magi of the Tribunal who strike him as ideal candidates to undertake the expedition. How will the characters react when a Redcap from Porta Pandere suggests that they meet in secret with the covenant's *princeps*, and they learn of his extraordinary offer?

### Resurgens

>**Lifespan:** 1151–Present<br>
>**Founders:** Farouk al-Ŷerbitonī, Zuleima al-Ŷerbitoniyya<br>
>**Season:** Summer<br>
>**Aura (type and strength):** Magic, strength 3<br>
>**Reputations:** Skilled Traders (Iberian Redcaps) 3<br>
>**Votes:** 4

The covenant of Resurgens is relatively recent, but it is destined to do great things in the near future. Established after the capture of Lisbon by crusaders from several kingdoms of Europe in 1147, the covenant has become, in less than a century of existence, a significant player in the city's political life, although its magi tread a path full of dangers.

#### History

The capture of Lisbon in 1147 brought about a radical change in the life of the city. Ruled until then by the Andalusis, the city was swiftly Christianized, and many of the crusaders came into possession of offices or lands in the city. One of them, Simon of Dover, obtained a large expanse of land near the banks of the Tagus. At that time a pair of Muslim Jerbiton magi from southwestern Iberia, Farouk and Zuleima, were in the city, completing their preparations to establish a covenant. The Jerbiton were forced to abandon their homes and hand over all their riches to the crusader troops when these entered the city, looting and wreaking havoc everywhere. Stripped of almost all their possessions and turned into Mudéjars, the magi approached Simon and offered to take the lands he had acquired off his hands in exchange for a Longevity Ritual. The crusader accepted, since he planned to leave for the Holy Land in any case, and soon the magi of Lisbon had a new home.

The lands acquired by the Jerbiton lay a short distance from the Muslim palace that would soon become the Castle of Saint George, and from the cathedral whose construction began after the capture of the city. They took out a loan from the Redcaps of Porta Pandere and ordered the construction of a building that would serve as residence, covenant and trading exchange. They named the covenant Resurgens because, although their earlier project had come to nothing, there had been moments during the capture of the city when they had given up even their lives for lost, and this was a second chance for them.

Resurgens soon caught the feverish activity that characterized Lisbon in the years after its reconquest. The Jerbiton were an important driving force in the city's commercial boom, taking an active part in numerous deals, almost always maritime, and gradually expanding their covenant until it became one of the leading trading houses of Lisbon, from which ships sailed carrying goods both east and north. Farouk and Zuleima knew how to use their magical abilities subtly to profit from almost every deal, while scrupulously respecting Hermetic law, thereby avoiding arousing any suspicion among the Quaesitores and, above all, among the Redcaps of Porta Pandere, who watched the covenant's prosperity with a mixture of admiration and envy.

Resurgens's activities have not been confined to trade in recent decades. Farouk, and even more so his *filia* Amira, have begun to use their wealth and influence to rub shoulders with the city's high nobility. Amira is prepared to do whatever it takes to make Lisbon the most important city in Portugal, going even further than her *parens*. Why not dream of making Lisbon the capital of the kingdom instead of Coimbra?

#### Setting and Physical Description

Resurgens occupies an extensive plot on the bank of the Tagus where it meets the sea at Lisbon, in the area called Alfama do Mar, a few hundred meters from the Castle of Saint George, in the commercial heart of the city. The covenant is divided into two large sections: on one side is the main building, a two-story stone structure housing the magi's *sancta* and the other chambers usual in a covenant, and on the other the trading exchange, an enormous hall where most commercial transactions take place, which also has a nearby wharf of its own from which ships sail with goods in which Resurgens has a direct interest.

Besides the *sancta*, the main structure contains the treasury and the magical library, all on the upper floor of a building whose façade is richly decorated with marbles brought from Italy and Mudéjar-style ornament. The ground floor is reserved for meeting rooms, the mundane library and, at the back, the barracks of the covenant's turb, which is not very large but is very well trained and equipped. As for the exchange, it is a great hall that only Farouk visits frequently, and from which shipments are prepared for various points of Mythic Europe.
<!-- p. 112 -->

The main building and the exchange are both joined by a tunnel that leads up the hillside to one of the underground pools of the Alfama quarter, the source of the covenant's magic aura. Its waters have magical properties: they always keep a warm, pleasant temperature that has healing effects on those who bathe in them. The waters also generate a small amount of Ignem vis that is very welcome to the covenant.

#### Society and Customs

The magi of Resurgens are governed by a strict bureaucracy, in which each of its members is in charge of a department or section of the covenant. The covenant currently has four departments, one for each magus: commercial relations, political relations, arcane affairs and military matters.

The present state of each department is a perfect reflection of the condition of the magus who runs it. Thus Farouk, despite his advanced age, remains as influential a figure in the commercial sphere as he was when Resurgens was founded, whereas Zuleima's cognitive decline in recent years has left the covenant's library and magical treasury somewhat neglected. The young and ambitious Amira handles political matters and, since passing her Gauntlet, has adopted a far more active stance than her predecessors. Finally, Alonso of Tremere is in charge of military matters.

Each magus manages his or her affairs independently, and all have complete confidence in the abilities of the others. They meet officially every three months to share the achievements of each department, but beyond that they have almost no direct contact unless it is essential. The one exception to this rule is, naturally, the case of Farouk and Zuleima, who share everything.

#### The Magi of Resurgens

##### Farouk al-Ŷerbitonī

The cofounder of Resurgens is over a hundred years old, but he remains in good shape thanks to a good Longevity Ritual and to not overusing magic in recent decades. He resorts to the Gift only when it is needed to complete transactions and close deals beneficial to the covenant, and with his mastery as a merchant that is less and less necessary. After several decades without leaving Lisbon, Farouk has begun to travel aboard the ships that sail from the banks of the Tagus, driven by the desire to see new and exotic places and, why not, to seek out new goods and products he can bring back to Lisbon at a profit.

> #### Cascais and Hell's Mouth
>
> Near Lisbon lies the small coastal town of Cascais, where the locals still whisper the old legend of Hell's Mouth. According to that legend, in ancient times a powerful and wicked sorcerer lived in a castle in the town. Eager to marry, the sorcerer searched the whole region for the most beautiful maiden, to whom he offered all manner of riches in exchange for her hand. The young woman refused and openly showed her contempt for the wizard, who, furious and mad with jealousy, kidnapped the maiden and locked her in the dungeons of his fortress. At the dungeon door he set a young knight as guard, with orders never to open the door and on no account to let out the maiden imprisoned there.
>
> The days went by and, little by little, curiosity began to get the better of the knight. He wondered who might be in there, what the maiden was like and why she was locked up. In the end his curiosity overcame him and he opened the door to see the prisoner with his own eyes. The two fell for each other and, over a series of secret trysts, a passionate love blossomed between them, until one day they decided to escape from the wizard's castle.
>
> It all happened on a stormy night. The knight and the young woman slipped through the castle's passages, went out into the courtyard where a horse awaited them, and fled at a gallop. But to their misfortune, the wizard noticed their flight and, as the two fugitives made their way along the nearby coast, he called upon his darkest powers to make the storm even more terrible and to split open the rock of the cliff beside which the couple was then fleeing. The dark chasm that opened swallowed the two lovers and their horse: they vanished forever.
>
> There is a version of the legend that differs a little from this one, holding that when the rocks opened, terrible demons summoned by the wizard emerged from within and dragged the two fugitives off to Hell itself.
>
> Be that as it may, the rocks of the coast never closed again, leaving a small cove surrounded by steep rock formations where, even today, the waves of the sea break with unusual violence. Gossips say that the screams of the two unfortunate lovers can still be heard as they are dragged away by the demons, although others say it is really nothing more than the noise of the wind whistling through the holes in the rocks. For this reason the locals of Cascais call the place Hell's Mouth.
>
> Ever since, the place has drawn all sorts of tormented or sinister individuals. Over the centuries many wretches have taken their own lives by throwing themselves onto the sharp rocks, and some pirates have even tried to use the place as a makeshift refuge, usually with disastrous consequences.
>
> Hell's Mouth has an Infernal aura of 4, which rises to 5 at night and also on certain unholy dates. If you set your saga in this area, bear in mind that in 1220 the king of Portugal, Afonso II, is excommunicated and the pope has threatened to place the kingdom under interdict, which infernal agents could exploit.

<!-- p. 113 -->

Farouk remains deeply in love with his wife Zuleima, despite all the time they have spent together. He is aware of his spouse's slow decline, but he tries to look the other way and ignore what it means both for the love of his life and for the covenant they began to build together. He knows that Final Twilight is not far off for her, but he intends to stay by her side until the very last moment, and he has even begun to consider leaving Lisbon with her while he still can, to see the countless places that Mythic Europe holds.

##### Zuleima al-Ŷerbitoniyya

Zuleima was always less adept than Farouk in commercial and mercantile matters, and so she left such maneuvers in her husband's hands while she devoted herself to creating and developing Resurgens's library and mundane treasury. It is she who has attended the Iberian Tribunals in recent decades, and she too who discovered both the vis source beneath the Alfama and the covenant's other sources. She has spent almost as much time studying and experimenting in her laboratory as accompanying her husband to social events, taking advantage of the Gentle Gift they both share, but lately she has been withdrawing more and more into her *sanctum*. The reason, known only to Farouk, is a series of Twilights the Jerbiton maga has undergone in recent years, which have begun to leave physical marks that are difficult to hide in the presence of mundanes.<br>
But the real damage Zuleima has suffered in those Twilights affects her mind and her ability to work magic. At times, Zuleima's mind switches off without warning when she uses some magical effect, leaving her sunk in a trance of indeterminate length. The maga remembers nothing of what happens during these trances, but lately they have become more frequent, which has given her an absolute terror of using any spell, however minor. This in turn has led her to neglect her responsibilities in the covenant, even forgetting to collect the vis from some of Resurgens's sources. For now only Farouk knows of her problems, but if the other magi became aware of them, the balance of power would shift entirely.

##### Amira al-Ŷerbitoniyya

Amira is a young maga of about forty who was trained by Farouk after he found her, when she was barely a child, at the underground spring of the Alfama, where she had come, drawn by the place's magic aura. She was an orphan with no home; Farouk sensed the Gift in the girl and decided to take her as his apprentice. During her fifteen years of apprenticeship, the Jerbiton polished the girl like a rough diamond, and although he never managed to rid her of certain remnants of her harsh childhood that have made her a ruthless and implacable adult, he did instill in her the philosophy that forms the foundations of the covenant. After brilliantly passing a complex Gauntlet that required her to settle a meeting between mundanes with wholly opposed interests without using her magic, Amira took over Resurgens's newly created department of political affairs, devoting herself body and soul to establishing cordial relations with the local nobility and even to controlling them as far as possible. Amira also has a gentler side that she strives to hide, which leads her to bring a romantic element into her political games, becoming infatuated from time to time with one or another of the most handsome Lisbon nobles.

##### Alonso of Tremere

Since its creation, Resurgens has had few hostile conflicts and has maintained good relations with the city's mundane powers, the Church included. At the end of the twelfth century, however, the Almohad caliph Abū Yaʿqūb Yūsuf launched an attack from the south to retake Lisbon. His troops got no further than the Setúbal area, on the outskirts of the city, but the magi of Resurgens realized that they had to strengthen their turb and their defenses. They spent a few years searching for a magus skilled in such matters, and soon they met Alonso, a Tremere from the north who was looking for a covenant in which to settle. In short order the Jerbiton had won him over and assigned him all matters of the covenant's military logistics.

Since his arrival, Alonso has turned the covenant's turb of grogs into professionals, making it a small but perfectly coordinated military unit, providing it with equipment of the finest quality and preparing it for any contingency. True to his Tremere mindset, he has reviewed all of Resurgens's structures, improving the magical defenses of the main building and even making sure that the covenant holds enough stores to survive for a time should the city suffer a siege like the one the crusaders laid less than a century ago. Alonso is a serious, professional magus, and a counterpoint to the Jerbiton with their constant social activity.

> #### Story Seeds: The Fountains of the Alfama
>
> The underground pool beneath Resurgens is part of a system of springs that runs through the whole subsoil beneath the Alfama quarter. Several of them have been discovered in recent decades, and the medicinal properties of some have reached the ears of the nobility. The king of Portugal himself, Afonso II, may be considering channeling these springs to supply water to the whole city, something that would be a blessing for its inhabitants. But... what would happen when that channeling reached the spring that connects directly with Resurgens? Will the Jerbiton manage to keep access to the spring and its vis, or will they have to give it up to keep their good relations with the city's mundane powers?

# V. The Kingdom of Leon

The kingdom of Leon is ruled by the powerful monarch Alfonso IX, who in 1220 is almost forty-nine years old. Alfonso was defeated at Alarcos, but he triumphed over the Almohad caliph at Las Navas de Tolosa, in a battle that changed the course of history forever. The father of many children, Alfonso keeps up a love affair with the Portuguese lady Teresa Gil de Soverosa, now pregnant with one of his future illegitimate daughters, Sancha Alfónsez. A year ago the Leonese monarch signed a peace treaty with the ever-contentious kingdom of Portugal, and he also set his signature beside that of his son, the young monarch of Castile, to prevent hostilities between their two kingdoms. In 1220, Alfonso is trying to stem the emigration of his subjects to other kingdoms and to hold back the bishops and nobles, whose power comes ever closer to that of the crown. In just a few months, Alfonso will lead a raid (*algara*) into the lands of Seville (capital of the Almohad province in the Peninsula) that will bring him great plunder in goods, gold and slaves.

The kingdom of Leon is washed by the Atlantic Ocean to the northwest and by the Cantabrian Sea to the north, and its commercial and maritime growth has encouraged the immigration of Franks and Englishmen, so in 1220 it is not unusual to find them in its port towns. To the west, Leon borders the kingdom of Portugal (from north to south, the town councils along its frontier include Bayona, Milmanda, Puebla, Fermoselle, Castelo Melhor and Sabugal, among others); to the east, Castile (from Llanes to Salvatierra, and from there to the Tagus); and to the south, the Almohad Empire (the border being marked by the line of the Tagus river, with Alcántara as the kingdom's southernmost town council).

## The Covenants of the Kingdom of Leon

The covenants are scattered among the kingdom's large regional units (from west to east and from north to south): Galicia, Asturias, the Bierzo, Leon, the Leonese Extremadura and the Transierra, all of them described in more detail below.
