<!-- p. 149 -->

The region of Castile borders on the Provençal Tribunal (indeed, the city of San Sebastián lies within the Provençal boundaries) and, as in any border region, disputes between Tribunals over the vis sources of the area are common. More than once the magi of Iberia have had to appear before the Provençal Tribunal, and no fewer disputes have had to be settled on Iberian soil. The storyguide should use this as a resource for creating stories that involve both Tribunals.

At present, the region of Castile is home to the covenants of Salionca and Pallantia, which coexist in relative harmony.

### Salionca

*Fire lies hidden in the stones. And as long as they do not strike together, it does not kindle.*[^p149-12]

[^p149-12]: Excerpt from *The Splendor of the Fruits of the Journey* by Ibn ʿArabī (Spanish translation by Carlos Varona Narvión).

>**Lifespan:** 780–Present<br>
>**Founders:** Grimoald Niger of Flambeau, Clodio of Flambeau, Gunthar of Flambeau<br>
>**Season:** Winter<br>
>**Aura (type and strength):** Magic, strength 8 (see below)<br>
>**Reputations:** Cursed (Castile) 3, Decadent (Order of Hermes) 2, Dictatorial (Iberian Tribunal) 2<br>
>**Votes:** 6

Salionca is the first covenant of Iberia (if Barzaj is not counted): it was formed a few years after the Founding of the Order and established at the first Rhine Tribunal. Because of its age, its origins have been mythologized over time through the passages of the *Comentarii de Bello Iberico* in which it is named. Thus, in 1220, many magi believe that Flambeau raised the covenant on the spot where Grimoald Niger slew Equión (king of the patarico giants), and that the giant's tears, as he died, salted the earth and created the vast, intermittent *regio* in which Salionca stands.

What was once the most powerful covenant of the Tribunal is now little more than a vast complex of empty chambers where very few magi wish to be; its inhabitants live under the effects of Warping and, when they die, end up turned into statues of salt. To magi newly arrived in the Tribunal, Salionca is nothing more than a cursed covenant in the twilight of an age that belongs to the past, while to those who knew its power and wealth, its fall is a promise to be celebrated and, why not, hastened.

Salionca has always been on good terms with the nobles of the kingdom of Castile. Indeed, until the Peripheral Code ruling "On Court Astronomers" (920) prohibited it, many of its members worked as astronomers to the monarchs, and since the end of the twelfth century it has been bound to the powerful house of Lara.

#### History

Flambeau conceived Salionca as a bastion for Hermetic expansion in the Peninsula. To that end, the magi Grimoald Niger, Clodio and Gunthar left Val-Negra and settled beside an ancient abandoned hillfort, not far from the Ebro, on the summit of a hill that commanded the surrounding landscape. They raised their covenant on an outcrop of salt from which a powerful and extensive magic aura emanated, and so they named their covenant Salionca.

Salionca was a prominent covenant during the early years of Hermetic history in the Peninsula, years that, as described in the *Comentarii de Bello Iberico* (see page 63), abounded in heroic deeds performed by Grimoald Niger. Later, figures such as the controversial Ruiz Sánchez de Esco (the one who refused to accept the *saḥirs* in 925) and the archmage Bruto of Flambeau, hero of the Schism War and Praeco of the Tribunal, helped to feed its fame. However, when Bruto announced his retirement because of a strange illness, Salionca vanished from Hermetic life and entered the Winter in which it still finds itself. The truth is that the *dictator* who replaced Bruto after his death, Marco Gayo of Flambeau (of Clodio's lineage), did not prove to have the abilities that Bruto had once seen in him.

Shortly after proclaiming himself *dictator* in 1185, Marco Gayo fell into Twilight during his contest for the title of archmage against the Tytalus of Duresca, Sepsis. Marco Gayo was struck down in the Cantabrian Mountains and, on the spot where he fell, his lover and former apprentice, Tito Octavio of Flambeau, raised a shelter to protect his body. In the absence of leadership, the triumvir Nuño Álvarez de Lara took over the government of Salionca, embezzling the covenant's resources to favor his family.

Unfortunately for Salionca, Nuño is Tito Octavio's only contact with the world, and the triumvir has made sure to hide from him that Salionca is on the brink of death. In recent years the triumvir has poured almost all of the covenant's funds into financing the civil war between the house of Burgundy (to which the king of Castile, Fernando III, belongs) and his own family's house, the Laras. Yet despite the fortune he sank into it, the Laras were defeated in 1217.

The embezzlement of the covenant's goods and its disastrous management drove the covenant's autocrat to leave, which in turn led many other inhabitants to go as well. So in these three years the covenant has lost almost its entire staff, and those who have not left are too affected by Warping to work. Without labor, the trade agreements with San Sebastián to sell salt in the city of Bruges (a voyage that takes six months) go unexploited, the cargoes that sailed down the Ebro have stopped, salt piles up in the storehouses, and the covenant's stony inhabitants cannot keep up. Moreover, to crown its misfortunes, none of the remaining mundanes is willing to take on the autocrat's work and responsibilities. In this situation, Nuño has begun negotiating with the Mercere of Aedes Saturni to sell them the distribution rights and one fifth of the working of Salionca's salt pans.

<!-- p. 150 -->

In 1220, however, the young maga Pyra has persuaded the Redcap who regularly visits the covenant to tell her about the agreements reached between the triumvir and House Mercere. To tackle the problem, Pyra has informed the other members at a secret assembly of the Decemvirate, which resolved to depose the triumvir before the summer of 1221 (when the ordinary Iberian Tribunal will be held and Nuño will sell the working rights to House Mercere). The decemvirs know, however, that Duresca is involved, so they do not rule out asking another covenant for help before the Tribunal is held.

#### Setting and Physical Description

Salionca is a covenant of monumental size. In its beginnings a single building was raised on the hill of the hillfort of the ancient Roman *civitas* of the same name, beside the river Oca, where there was a powerful magic aura that, wherever it rose to the surface, made salt spring from the earth. The whole area is full of salt pans, whose origin has been closely studied by the magi of Salionca, who have written numerous treatises on the subject.

Over time the covenant grew. The original site is still preserved as the council chamber and is large enough to hold an ordinary Tribunal. Although the members of the covenant have also used this chamber to hold their councils, it is now too open and cold a space, so the members meet in a smaller adjoining hall that the Quaesitores used to use during the ordinary Tribunals. Beneath these buildings lies the Hermes portal *Quintus*, guarded by an ominous automaton created at the end of the tenth century by a Verditius master from the covenant of Ajabeba. Today, however, the automaton does not work properly, as its maintenance has been neglected, so a group of grogs guards the portal. As with the rest of the buildings, the walls are covered in saline growths, and in some places the stone itself has turned into a huge block of salt because of Warping. In fact, the hill on which the council chamber stands has a whitish coloring around the building's foundations.

The next most important building is the impressive structure that houses the magi's *sancta*, Salionca's treasure chamber and the pantheon of the *dictatores* (see below). For its protection, it was raised by magic in the shelter of the gorges of the river Oca. Its rooms rise impossibly from the sheer walls of the river cliffs, a sight that bears witness to Salionca's former might. Of the fifteen *sancta* in this building, only six are currently occupied. Here too the salt devours the rooms, turning them into uninviting, extremely dry chambers where at times it is hard to breathe. Warping affects not only the structures, however, but also the walls of the gorge: the surrounding rock is turning into salt which, being more brittle, has weakened the anchorage of the old buildings. For this reason, two of the *sancta* have already partly collapsed. The magi still remember with horror how the aged Jew Elifaz of Flambeau ended up crushed against the riverbed after an earth tremor hurled the first *sanctum* into the void in 1170.

<!-- p. 151 -->

The rest of Salionca's buildings (three small villages) oversee the working of the magical salt pans and are spread over a radius of up to a hundred kilometers north of the covenant's *sancta* building, and even farther if one counts the fishing rights of the old covenant of Izaro, which Salionca still controls (see below).

At the end of the eleventh century the covenant reached the largest population in its history: Salionca came to be home to more than 1,000 people. Today, however, it does not have even 200 inhabitants on its rolls, all of them deeply affected by the aura's Warping.

#### The Covenant's Pantheon

As mentioned above, the *dictatores* of Salionca have the honor (and the obligation) of being buried in the covenant's pantheon and, along with them, all their weapons, riches, books, magic items and talismans. Unfortunately, many of the *dictatores* met their Final Twilight before leaving office (as is the case with the covenant's founder, Grimoald Niger), so all that remains of them is an empty niche and whatever belongings they did not take with them.

Only the *dictatores* have the right to set foot in this sacred precinct, and only they know what the pantheon holds: possibly countless riches, books, vis and enchantments accumulated over more than four centuries. Much of Salionca's power lies in this secret and, were it revealed, its enemies could estimate its resources and judge precisely how to finish off the covenant.

#### The Aura of Salionca

Both the magi's building and Salionca's council chamber are steeped in a powerful magic aura of level 8. Unfortunately for its inhabitants, at some point in the eleventh century the aura began to surface in the other locations, inflicting Warping on the mundane workers of the salt pans. The first symptoms appeared in the buildings: saltpeter growths began to appear in the corners where walls met, then spread to the walls and ceilings, and finally broke through the floor.

As the years go by, the buildings are slowly transformed into blocks of saltpeter, and the mundanes gradually lose mobility and grow stiffer: their bodies turn to salt with age until, finally, they become statues of salt. Although this gives them a natural defense, it also makes them sluggish and, above all, frightens them. Some of the inhabitants left Salionca when Warping began to show in many of the salt-pan workers, but the autocrat of the time managed to persuade almost all of them to stay. Since his departure, however, those whose Warping was not yet strong enough to quench their desire to leave have gone as well. Today the covenant is peopled by men and women of salt who barely move, toiling painfully in the mines or slowly patrolling the halls of the covenant's main buildings (see insert on the previous page).

> #### The Grogs of Salionca
>

Although the hardening of their skin keeps them from moving quickly, they are tough and loyal fighters. Below are the statistics of a standard Salionca soldier. >**Appearance:** The soldiers of Salionca are imposing and fearsome, chosen from among the strongest and most intelligent children of the covenant. These grogs have taken part in numerous mundane battles against the neighboring kingdoms (above all defending the interests of the Laras), and so they are formidable warriors. Being affected by Warping, they are long-lived and show no infirmities; when they offer themselves for combat, they are like living statues that seem to feel neither fatigue nor pain. When the inhabitants of Salionca die, they turn into statues of salt, and a pawn of Ignem vis can be found in their bodies.

<!-- p. 152 -->

In game terms, the aura follows the rules of the Warping to a Pattern Hook (see *Covenants*, page 15): the mineral kingdom within the aura is gradually transformed into rock salt (halite) and saltpeter, and the other kingdoms (vegetable and animal) are transmuted in the same way, though more slowly. In the tenth century one of the members of Salionca, Birbón of Flambeau, devoted many years to researching the aura. In his studies he concluded that the place would end up turning into one enormous salt pan, and he prophesied that at that moment the giants of the Peninsula would return.

In game terms, the Flaws (all of supernatural origin) that the aura of Salionca grants to mundanes are as follows: Arthritis (on reaching a Warping Score of one), because of the hardening of the joints; Social Handicap (on reaching a Warping Score of three), because the skin turns whitish with pinkish iridescence; and Soul of Salt (on reaching a Warping Score of five; see "New Virtues and Flaws," page 305).

#### Society and Customs

Founded as a democracy by Grimoald Niger, who is nominally regarded as the first *dictator*, Salionca is now an autocracy that uses the mechanisms of a hierarchical organization to make decisions; the hierarchy is very strict, and *certamen* cannot be used to settle any dispute relating to Salionca (as set down in its charter).

Salionca has four legislative chambers able to decide on their own affairs. However, any member of higher rank may attend the lower chambers to cast a vote and exercise authority (that is, the *dictator* may attend any other meeting and take its resolutions to the *Comitia Centuriata* to submit them to a private hearing).

- ***Comitia Centuriata*:** this assembly seats the *dictator* and the *magister equitum*, the highest authorities in the government of Salionca.
- **Triumvirate:** the governing assembly of the three triumvirs (up to three seats).
- **Decemvirate:** the governing assembly of the decemvirs (up to ten seats).
- **Curia:** the governing assembly of the rest of the covenant's inhabitants, mostly mundanes. This assembly is presided over by the covenant's autocrat, who has the final word on any decision this chamber makes.

The *dictator* is the highest authority in Salionca; his vote counts double and he may submit any decision to a private hearing of the *Comitia Centuriata* (which *de facto* means he can make any decision unilaterally). In addition, he has the right of veto over any number of votes cast by the Triumvirate, and he may promote or demote any member of the covenant. The *dictator* receives the largest allocation of magical and mundane resources, and has the right to live in the *sanctum* of Grimoald Niger (possibly the most opulent in the entire Iberian Tribunal) and to enter the covenant's pantheon. In the past the *dictator* had to be an archmage, but Bruto repealed that clause of the charter so that Marco Gayo could take the office.

The *magister equitum* is the *dictator*'s general, his right hand and the one charged with leading the covenant's militias in battle. The *magister equitum* may annul up to two votes of the Triumvirate and up to six votes of the Decemvirate (provided they do not support what the *dictator* has pronounced). In the *dictator*'s absence, he is obliged to take the reins of the covenant, although he has no right to use the *dictator*'s *sanctum* or to enter the covenant's pantheon.

The triumvirs are a group of up to three magi. They are charged with conducting the covenant's lesser affairs, so they may call councils on such matters without the *Comitia Centuriata* present, and they have authority over the chamber of the Decemvirate: each triumvir may annul up to three votes of the Decemvirate, provided those votes are not aligned with the *dictator*'s. Each triumvir has one vote, and their chamber may propose matters for approval by the *Comitia Centuriata*. Should the *Comitia Centuriata* stand empty, the triumvirs may govern the covenant. Indeed, on one occasion the members of the Triumvirate decided not to be promoted to the *Comitia Centuriata* so as to govern the covenant more democratically, although this prevented them from using the *sanctum* of Grimoald Niger and from entering the covenant's pantheon. Finally, the triumvirs are responsible for casting the *Aegis of the Hearth*.

The decemvirs make up the assembly of the Decemvirate and are ten in number. This assembly may propose new matters to the Triumvirate and governs the Curia, so it may pass any opinion on to the autocrat for him to regulate the running of the covenant's mundanes.

#### Promotion in Salionca

All magi who join the covenant start in the Decemvirate. To gain access to the Triumvirate, decemvirs must have spent at least twenty-one years in the covenant. Only then may they apply for promotion to the Triumvirate, in which there must also be a free seat.

To gain access to the *Comitia Centuriata*, a triumvir must have sat in the Triumvirate for at least fourteen years. Promotion is always proposed by the *Comitia Centuriata*, so it usually happens when the *magister equitum* is promoted to *dictator* and his seat falls vacant.

The promotion of the *magister equitum* to *dictator* is made by direct appointment by the *dictator*. That is, if the *dictator*'s throne falls empty before a successor has been chosen, the *magister equitum* cannot sit on it except by a joust in the arena. To do so, the *magister equitum* must declare Wizard's War on each of the members of the Triumvirate and emerge victorious from every one of them. Naturally, this process could leave the *dictator*'s seat empty for years.

Besides the mechanisms described for rising to power in Salionca, the covenant's members may always resort to usurpation, the means by which they can gain an occupied seat of higher rank: to do so, the petitioner must declare Wizard's War on the magus he wishes to overthrow.

<!-- p. 153 -->

#### The Magi of Salionca

##### Dictator Marco Gayo of Flambeau

*Friend, arise, for it is late — have we been keeping vigil all this time? But he said to me: "We cannot rise; the earth still lies upon us." Do you remember a night in its shade, when the days were a feast? How much joy poured down upon us then, like abundant rain! All has passed as if it had never been, and misfortune now is present.*[^p153-13]

[^p153-13]: Poem by Ibn Shuhayd written on his tomb, from *The Treatise of Familiar Spirits and Demons* (Spanish translation by S. Barberá).

Marco Gayo is the covenant's *dictator*. He was appointed to the office by Bruto of Flambeau when he was only a triumvir, so he had to face and defeat the former *magister equitum* in a Wizard's War, which he survived only thanks to Bruto. Once his rival was defeated, however, Marco Gayo did not dare take the office of *magister equitum*, for he felt he was not ready to assume it.

Bruto chose Marco Gayo as his successor for his measured temperament and his diplomacy. With the arrival of the Almohads, the last thing Bruto wanted was for the Order to go to war again, for, in his own words, they had enough to deal with in the folly of the Praeco of the Tribunal at the time, Munio Alfonso Garcés al-Flambī, of the covenant of Harra. But when Bruto was laid low by his illness, Marco Gayo did not dare usurp his office, and the covenant began to languish for lack of leadership. Matters did not improve when Bruto turned into a statue of salt and Marco buried him in the covenant's pantheon: the new *dictator* proved a weak leader, and the triumvirs ended up challenging him. In fact, they would have deposed him had it not been for the intervention of the then decemvir Nuño Álvarez de Lara, who enabled him to close an advantageous pact with the Laras that placated the triumvirs. In gratitude, Marco gave him the vacant seat in the Triumvirate and, over time, began to delegate to him most of the tasks of governing the covenant. In this way Marco Gayo was able to devote himself to teaching his first apprentice, Tito Octavio, with whom he fell hopelessly in love. And so, when Tito Octavio became a magus, Marco Gayo appointed him *magister equitum*.

A few years later, Marco Gayo discovered that he was suffering from the same illness as Bruto, so he linked the affliction to the office and, although he told no one, he made Tito Octavio swear never to claim the post of *dictator*. It was then that his *amicus* and confidant, Nuño Álvarez, persuaded him to challenge Sepsis of Tytalus for the title of archmage. And that is how the hoplite sent him into a Twilight from which he has still not emerged.

##### Magister Equitum Tito Octavio of Flambeau

*Fulfilling one's obligations is a painful duty for every reasonable person, and to long for the past, and not to forget what once was and is now beyond remedy, is the surest sign of true loyalty.*[^p153-14]

[^p153-14]: Excerpt from *The Ring of the Dove* by Ibn Ḥazm (Spanish translation by Emilio García Gómez).

Tito Octavio has not left the body of his lover, Marco Gayo, since he found it on the high Cantabrian peaks. To shield it from the harsh weather, Tito had a shelter built where he could keep vigil over his former master. With hardly any experience, Tito found himself obliged to delegate all his power to his *parens*'s *amicus*, Nuño, in whom he trusts completely. Since then Tito has barely left the shelter, for fear of not being at his lover's side when he wakes. He cares little for the covenant, for he cannot help recalling the years when he was happy at Marco Gayo's side; compared with that happiness, the rest of the world is nothing but a gray smudge.

In 1220, Tito realizes that many of his requests are postponed indefinitely and that he obtains practically nothing of what he asks for, so he suspects that the covenant must be going through a bad time — which, to tell the truth, does not worry him much either. Yet every year that passes makes it more likely that his lover has met Final Twilight, so he is determined to attend the Tribunal of 1221 to obtain the help needed to bring Gayo back (see insert on page 154).

##### Triumvir Nuño Álvarez de Lara of Flambeau, Follower of Apromor

Of the house of Lara, Nuño Álvarez helped the *dictator* to consolidate his power when the triumvirs challenged him. Thanks to his skillful maneuvering, Nuño managed to take one of the three chairs of the Triumvirate and, displaying a great lack of scruples, got the other two triumvirs to leave for the covenant of Harra. Without them, Nuño had a free hand to wield his power and, why not, to profit from it.

After getting the *dictator* to challenge Sepsis, Nuño began meeting with the leaders of his family to plan the usurpation of the throne of Castile; he knew that Marco Gayo could not defeat the archmage, but he never imagined he could survive, even if only through Twilight. Although the decemvirs consider him a cruel person, Nuño does not see himself that way.

Having invested all of Salionca's funds in a lost war for control of the throne of Castile, and accepting that Salionca will never leave its Winter, Nuño has reached an agreement with Aedes Saturni and Duresca. In exchange for the distribution rights and one fifth of the working of Salionca's salt pans, the Tribunal's coffers will rebuild the covenant of Harra and, after Nuño takes the office of *dictator*, he will dissolve Salionca and be named *ductor* of the new Harra. To further his interests, since 1217 Nuño has canceled all assemblies and forbidden the decemvirs to meet, in the hope that the Tribunal of 1221, when the agreement will be sealed, arrives without upsets.

##### Decemvir Pyra of Flambeau

The decemvir Pyra is Salionca's only hope. Of the whole assembly of the Decemvirate, Pyra is the most experienced maga and the one with the most initiative. Having learned of Nuño's maneuvers, Pyra plans to neutralize him before he closes the deal with the Mercere of Aedes Saturni. Pyra knows her limitations, however: Nuño is an aged magus with far more experience than she has, and if she challenged him to a Wizard's War she would end up dead at best. For this reason, the maga is willing to ask another covenant for help if necessary (the characters' covenant would be a good choice), although if she has no other option, she does not rule out facing the triumvir alone.

##### Decemvir Rescaldo of Flambeau

The young Rescaldo is the *filius* of Birbón, one of the triumvirs who left for Harra and who perished at the battle of Alarcos (see page 94). Rescaldo is not very interested in politics and spends his seasons enjoying Salionca's magnificent library and improving his Arts, in the hope of fighting the Almohads one day. Despite his apparent indifference, Rescaldo supports Pyra, for he knows the consequences the deal Nuño intends to close may bring. If Salionca disappeared he would lose his home and, besides, who would not want to save the oldest covenant in the Tribunal, founded by Flambeau himself?

> #### Story Seeds: The Return of Marco Gayo
>
> The first part of the *Comentarii de Bello Iberico* recounts the popular episode in which Clodio of Flambeau, Grimoald's companion, goes to Mount Anboto to wage war on the divinity that dwells there and so win its vis sources. In the verses, Clodio enters a cave carved into the eastern face of the mountain, where he finds the refuge of a divinity of the ancient world known as Mariurrika Kobea. The tale describes her as a young woman who is forever combing out her hair with a golden comb. In their encounter, Clodio must use the wind to decipher the divinity's language, and her words are so powerful that they make his ears bleed. In the narrative, the deity's message, rendered in prose, is as follows:
>
> *Defeat the mairuak giants to force them to raise a temple where I may rest; settle the truth of the eternal quarrel between my sons, Mikelatz and Atarrabi; and, lastly, free my daughter Llargui from the god of darkness Gaueko, for every twenty-eight days he shuts her away beneath his cloak, and my offspring are left helpless, with no light to guide their steps when the souls walk wandering upon the earth*.
>
> Tito Octavio believes this passage is true and suspects that Clodio could not overcome the trials, since the *Comentarii de Bello Iberico* never mentions the matter again. And although many magi have returned to Anboto, no one has found the entrance the book describes, so it is considered a myth.
>
> At the Tribunal of 1221, Salionca's *magister equitum* approaches the player characters to ask for their help. Recalling the passage above, he begs them to climb Anboto and place themselves at the service of the goddess Maddi so that they may demand from her the return of Marco Gayo. In exchange, Tito Octavio will offer them anything: vis sources, magical resources, riches — even the office of *dictator* itself!
>
> Will they manage to overcome her trials? And if they do, will they ask for the return of Marco Gayo, or will they request something else in exchange? What if the trials had already been overcome by another magus in the past? Perhaps Maddi will set them other challenges, or show herself hostile toward them.

##### Decemvir Focus of Flambeau, Follower of Apromor

Focus is the youngest magus in Salionca. He came to the covenant in 1195, after being expelled from Harra for refusing to go to Alarcos. Although Nuño approved his admission, it was Pyra who won him over to her side. Together with Pyra, he is the only member who would give his life for Salionca, but he is too immature to be any match for the triumvir Nuño.

### Pallantia, Studium Generale

*How great is the blindness of ignorance, and how dangerous!*[^p155-15]

[^p155-15]: Excerpt from *The Guide for the Perplexed* by Maimonides (Spanish translation by David Gonzalo Maeso).

>**Lifespan:** 1151–Present<br>
>**Founders:** Aldonza Ierbitonis de Careluega, Osoro of Bonisagus de Burgos<br>
>**Season:** Spring<br>
>**Aura (type and strength):** Magic, strength 1<br>
>**Reputations:** Mundane Pacts (Iberian Tribunal) 6, *Studium generale* (Mythic Europe) 4<br>
>**Votes:** 2

The *studium generale* of Pallantia (see insert on page 55) is the most recent covenant in the kingdom of Castile. Yet despite its seventy years of existence, it has still not managed to leave behind a Spring that seems to threaten to turn into a premature Winter.

Its founder, a follower of the Muslim and Jewish "educational models" of the Peninsula, chose a broken key as its symbol to show that there is no need to uncover what is not hidden.

#### History

When Aldonza conceived the project for her covenant, she knew it was risky, for she meant to take root in a mundane institution (the Church, no less) and grow together with it. Because of this, it took her four years to find Osoro (a former acolyte): the only person who dared to found the covenant with her in 1151.

The creation of Pallantia revitalized the cathedral school of Palencia. Aldonza and Osoro managed to attract great masters of theology and the liberal arts to the school and, for almost half a century, turned Pallantia into a place to which *parentes* could send their apprentices to receive basic formal schooling before becoming magi, in exchange for a token payment of vis. Pallantia also fostered some early discoveries of Gifted children, and at the ordinary Tribunal of 1200 the covenant obtained the status of dedicated covenant for the promotion of Hermetic education in Iberia, for which it received a certain magical and mundane remuneration to carry out its task.

<!-- p. 156 -->

> #### Atomist Magic Theory
>
> *To weary minds with questions that exceed their capacity, while lacking even the proper instruments, betrays a want of sound judgment and a kind of madness.*[^p156-VII]
>
> When Osoro was made a magus in 1144, he was obsessed with the theory of atoms set out by Democritus and reformulated by Epicurus. During his years of apprenticeship and maturity he read numerous Arabic treatises on its principles and, drawing on them and on Aristotle's elemental laws, he renamed the Forms and Techniques and reduced their number. In this way Osoro managed to reformulate the foundations of a new magic theory according to the following principles:
>
> - All matter is made up of indivisible particles of fixed mass; these particles belong to each of the four elements that compose all bodies and their attributes, namely fire, air, water and earth. These so-called atoms are identical if they belong to the same kind, and therefore there is no difference whatsoever between them.
>
> - Atoms are uncreated and therefore eternal.
>
> - All matter comes into being, takes shape and decays according to the atomic processes of aggregation, separation, motion and rest.
>
> - For atoms to be able to move, join together (to generate matter) or come apart (to break it down), the void must exist.
>
> Osoro reduced the Forms to four *atomi*: *atomus ignis*, *atomus terrae*, *atomus aurae* and *atomus aquae*; and he turned the Techniques into the four fundamental processes by which the *atomi* are manipulated: *unio* (join), *discindo* (break apart), *moveo* (move) and *quiesco* (halt). He has not yet managed to stabilize his discoveries, however; manipulating matter in this way is extremely costly in vis for him, however minute the process involved, but he can do things that lie beyond Hermetic capabilities and their limits, although his theory also carries new limits of its own, such as the impossibility of creating new atoms.
>
> For now, Osoro has shared his findings only with Marŷān (of Dār Malīḥaʾ), who has pointed out their importance. His new theory, however, carries certain logical and theological implications that clash with the foundations of the known world: first, it holds matter to be eternal (in accordance with Aristotle), since he has never once managed to create *atomi*, which refutes the creation of the world and therefore that there was a beginning; second, if what exists is eternal and uncreated, it refutes the existence of creation and attacks the existence of God. Likewise, he cannot fit the existence of the four realms into his postulate; they do not even interfere with his new theory, but deep down he knows he cannot dismiss them. These conclusions have forced him to set his studies aside, and he is all but ready to surrender before the limits of his intellect. Despite Marŷān's insistence, he does not dare publish his results, for they refute Aristotle's teleological providence and call into question the criticisms Maimonides makes of the atomists in *The Guide for the Perplexed*.
>
> [^p156-VII]: Excerpt from *The Guide for the Perplexed* by Maimonides (Spanish translation by David Gonzalo Maeso).

In 1212 Pallantia received a generous endowment from King Alfonso VIII of Castile and was granted the title of *studium generale*. Domingo de Guzmán (founder of the Order of Preachers) had been educated in its classrooms, and every year eminent scholars from every corner of Mythic Europe came to teach at Pallantia. However, the Quaesitores of Duresca began to investigate it, for Alfonso VIII's generous donation made them suspicious of Aldonza.

The year 1214 was a terrible one for Pallantia. In light of the suspicions raised by the Quaesitores, the Tribunal voted in full session to strip it of its status as a dedicated covenant, fined it for its mundane dealings and forbade it from continuing to negotiate with the crown. Moreover, in the autumn of that same year Alfonso VIII, the great protector of the *studium generale* of Palencia, died. As a result, the covenant sank into a grave financial crisis, and many of the teachers began to leave for the cathedral school of Salamanca after Alfonso IX of Leon granted it the title of *studium generale* in 1218.

Despite everything, Aldonza and Osoro go on working for Pallantia; their goal is to keep educating their students, and they devote all their efforts to it. But the slander the Redcaps have spread about it has stemmed the flow of Hermetic teachers who came to its classrooms every year, and the magi of the Tribunal do not want to risk sending their apprentices to a covenant with such a bad name either. As if that were not enough, almost all the great masters prefer to go to Salamanca, so the *studium generale* of Palencia is all but abandoned.

#### Setting and Physical Description

Pallantia is set on the main street of Palencia, a few meters from the Visigothic cathedral of San Antolín and very close to the Carrión river. The building has two stories and is arranged around a courtyard from which one can climb to the classrooms where lessons are given. The portico leading into the courtyard is of stone, and the building's façade is decorated with twelve lambs in a palm grove, adorned with no few Hermetic motifs.

The *studium generale* complex has a chapel where students may go to pray at any time, and rooms that can be rented throughout the school year. The *sancta* of Aldonza and Osoro lie near the river, where they enjoy a weak *lacuna* in which they can carry out their magical research without being hampered by the powerful Divine aura of the city.

<!-- p. 157 -->

#### Society and Customs

The covenant of Pallantia is perfectly integrated into the city and mundane society; although it is part of the Order, it ultimately answers to the cathedral chapter of San Antolín.

Although the founders have always been able to reconcile their Hermetic lives with their teaching, since 1214 Aldonza and Osoro have had to teach full time. As teachers they are great communicators (although Aldonza must go disguised as a man at all times), and they have managed to make up for the loss they have suffered since, in 1218, Salamanca took most of their teaching staff.

Although many find it strange, neither Aldonza nor Osoro has had apprentices. They have handed all the Gifted children they have found over to other masters, in the hope that one of them might return once made a magus. So far, however, this has never happened, and Pallantia is growing old with no guarantee of renewal.

As for the students, they always hold a celebration on graduating, at which family and teachers gather in Pallantia's great hall to talk and drink all day long. At night, however, the celebration goes on, to the embarrassment of the canons who live in the covenant. Then, the next morning, Aldonza uses magic to imprint the names of the graduates on the west wall that faces the river, and on nights without moon or stars their traces faintly light the covenant's garden. For Aldonza and Osoro it is a source of true pride to contemplate them.

Although there is no hierarchy in Pallantia, Aldonza holds the title of *decanus* of the covenant (as its spokesperson at Tribunals), and Osoro that of *professor*.

#### The Magae of Pallantia

##### Decanus Aldonza Ierbitonis de Careluega

Aldonza is an aged maga with the Gentle Gift who is very close to her Final Twilight. Her situation has grown worse over the last six years, since in order to teach she has had to disguise herself as a man by magic. The constant use of MuIm spells is giving her Warping, which only makes her already delicate situation worse. Although Osoro has asked her to retire, Aldonza is unwilling to abandon her duties merely because she is exposed to a second source of Warping.

As the driving force behind Pallantia, all she wants is to see its classrooms full of young men again. Many nights she walks through the covenant's gardens, contemplating the long list of names of those who have left Pallantia, and wonders how the Order can be so foolish: "Will no one help us? Is there no one who values our work?"

Aldonza knows that Osoro is sacrificing himself for her; he is a brilliant man, and it grieves her to see him give up his studies for the sake of teaching and the withered dream of Pallantia. Aldonza is aware of the letters Osoro receives every year with offers from other covenants and, although she knows it is a selfish feeling, she wishes with all her heart that Osoro will not leave, for that would mean the end of the covenant.

<!-- p. 158 -->

### Professor Osoro of Bonisagus of Burgos

Osoro is a mature magus who has devoted his whole life to the study of Hermetic theory and who, like Aldonza, has the Gentle Gift. Many in Iberia consider him a genius, and they are not wrong: Osoro was the true architect of the pact with Alfonso, which brought Pallantia a brief Summer and also brought down the fines of the Quaesitores. Osoro, however, is neither ambitious nor spiteful, so he does not believe in revenge, nor has he any interest in proving his innocence, for there is no need to prove what anyone versed in logic could easily deduce.

Since 1218 he has had to set aside his Hermetic research (see insert on page 155), on which he was working together with Marŷān al-Bonisagiyya of Dār Malīḥaʾ, because teaching takes up all his time. In response, his colleague has asked him to leave, and although Osoro knows that Pallantia's days are numbered, he cannot bring himself to abandon Aldonza. And so the man many Iberian scholars regard as the new Isidore spends his days humbly teaching the students who arrive each year in the lecture halls of the Palencia *studium generale*.

> #### Story Seeds: Atomist Magic Theory
>
> Marŷān comes to the ordinary Tribunal of 1221 expecting to find Osoro, but no representative of Pallantia is there. Carried away by enthusiasm, she sets out the principles of the *studium generale* master's research before a small gathering that includes the player characters' magi. According to her, "the new magic theory does away with the limits that Bonisagus artificially established." Perhaps this news will only deepen the Tribunal's mistrust of Pallantia, or perhaps it will arouse the characters' curiosity and lead them to learn the true situation of the covenant. They might then decide to help its magi or — why not? — to denounce them to the ecclesiastical authorities of Palencia, for is Osoro not, perhaps, an atheist?

### Tertia

>**Lifespan:** 843–1046<br>
>**Founder:** Átropo of Tremere<br>
>**Aura (type and strength):** Magic, strength 5<br>
>**Reputations:** Shameful (Iberian Tribunal) 3, Dishonorable (Iberian Tremere) 2

The covenant of Tertia was officially constituted at the Rhine Tribunal of 843 and, like Secunda, formed part of the Tremere's hegemonic plan.

#### History

Tertia was founded by the Hermetic sister of Somnus, for both had been trained at Lycaneon by Erebus *filius* Tremere. Her arrival was part of Tremere's master plan to dominate the Order. With Átropo as *rector* of Tertia and Somnus as *rector* of Secunda, the Tremere network of influence took firm hold on the western edge of the Order.

Átropo established good relations with the Qasī of Arnedo, from whom she obtained permission to build an impressive covenant in a gentle ravine of Viejo Cameros, near the Qasī family seat. Throughout her life the maga systematically violated the Code in pursuit of her own interests, and although all the covenant's records were destroyed after the Sundering, the magi of the Peninsula came to learn of some of her deeds.

- In 844, with the Qasī at the height of their power, Átropo turned the clashes between Asturias and al-Andalus to her advantage. When the armies of Ramiro I fought the troops of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān II at Clavijo (to abolish the tribute of the hundred maidens), the Tremere intervened in the fighting and handed victory to the Christian forces in exchange for a handsome reward.

- A year later, in 845, she induced Ramiro I to decree the burning of every wizard in his kingdom, ridding herself of the troublesome Tancoystl Ex Miscellanea and provoking a far from modest Hermetic migration to the south of the Peninsula.

- Finally, in 848, she became embroiled in the Sundering and, although Átropo was neutralized like the rest of Tremere's lieutenants, Tertia was the only Tremere covenant of the Tribunal to survive beyond that day.

> #### Story Seeds: The Dragon's Footprints
>
> Tertia's most important vis source came from the petrified footprints of an ancient dragon. If the first snows that settled in them were gathered, the magi of Tertia could extract a large quantity of Vim vis.
>
> With Tertia's fall, the sources passed into the possession of Salionca, which has stopped harvesting them in recent years. If the player characters were to find out, they could try to exploit them. Furthermore, if Salionca were eventually to disappear, the source would become theirs. Of course, the characters need not know of the pact that Aedes Saturni and Duresca have made with Salionca, which could lead to an interesting situation between the characters' covenant and two of the most powerful covenants of the Tribunal.

<!-- p. 159 -->

After Átropo's death, the Asturian nobility granted the rights to Clavijo to Fata *filia* Átropo of Tremere, who took the reins of Tertia after the Sundering. Fata continued the established policy toward the Qasī, so that when the Tremere of Tremébriga (Acutus and Tremula Flamma) arrived, she persuaded Musā ibn Musā to sell them a plot of his lands on which to build their covenant. With the founding of Tremébriga, however, Tertia was relegated to second place. Among its duties, Tertia was charged with maintaining relations with the Qasī, but when Musā's weak son, Lubb, swore allegiance to Ordoño I of Asturias, Tremébriga forced Tertia to concentrate on the Asturian Christians. In this way Fata succeeded in gaining the fortress of Clavijo and all its domains, which brought her great profit and influence.

Tertia's light was extinguished, however, by the Schism War, in which all its members perished except for a very young maga who had passed her Gauntlet barely five years earlier. Tertia's influence in the area dwindled until, in 1033, the king of Pamplona seized the fortress of Clavijo and gave all its lands to the monastery of San Martín de Albelda. Thus Tertia, which had held the rights to exploit roads, bridges, vineyards, meadows and mills, was stripped of all its wealth. This, together with its losses in the Schism War, plunged it into a harsh Winter, which ended when Salionca accused it of having maintained mundane ties with the monastery of San Martín. At the ordinary Tribunal of 1046, Duresca sentenced its very young *rector* to pay a heavy fine or be expelled from the Tribunal. Unable to pay, the last heir of the Tremere implicated in the Sundering left Iberia, and Tertia was abandoned.

#### Setting and Physical Description

For the Tremere of the Peninsula, the memory of Tertia has always been a stain, so they have made no effort to recover or preserve its halls. For the rest of the magi, Tertia is a byword for villainy, so although it lies within a powerful aura, hardly anyone would dare to occupy a place with such a reputation (though in truth it would make settling easier for any Spring covenant wishing to take its first steps in the Tribunal).

The ruins of Tertia are hard to find, since nature has swallowed them, although the old walls of the buildings still stand (the wooden roofs and floors do not). The covenant's wealth and library were seized by Duresca and Salionca, and its vis sources shared out. Today nothing of interest remains at Tertia for the magi of the Peninsula.

### Izaro

>**Lifespan:** 899–982<br>
>**Founders:** Geralla of Apromor, Vitalis of Apromor<br>
>**Aura (type and strength):** Magic, strength 5<br>
>**Reputations:** None

Originally founded as a chapter house of Salionca, Izaro (from the Basque, pronounced *isaro*) never managed to break free of its mother covenant and remained subordinate to it until its destruction.

#### History

When, in the mid-ninth century, the magi of Salionca discovered the abundant vis sources around the estuary of the Oca river (an ancient place of power of the Asturian vates), they sent a detachment to gather the vis locally, since harvesting it required a complex method involving the use of magic.

When Geralla of Salionca volunteered, she took her apprentice Vitalis with her. She met numerous mundane obstacles to settling in the area, however, until, thanks to her diplomatic skills, she struck an agreement with Jaun Zuria, grandson of the king of Scotland: if she helped him drive the Castilians out of Biscay, he would give her a plot of land on which to build her covenant. To seal the pact, Geralla took part in the battle of Arrigorriaga, where, it is said, so many men died that every stone on the ground was stained red. After the victory, Jaun Zuria was named lord of Biscay and gave Geralla the island on which she founded Izaro.

Izaro never had more than two magi in its ranks; subordinate as it was to the government of Salionca, its votes were cast as a bloc at Tribunals.

<!-- p. 160 -->

At the beginning of the tenth century, Izaro became an important whaling port that helped to enrich Salionca still further. In 941, while the rest of the Tribunal was in turmoil over the Duresca manuscripts, Geralla tried to separate Izaro from Salionca. To do so, she took advantage of the period of instability Salionca was going through (the *Comitia Centuriata* was deserted, and barely a year had passed since the expelled and infamous *dictator* Ruiz Sánchez of Flambeau had been murdered) and challenged the only triumvir left in the covenant to Wizard's War. Unfortunately for Izaro, Geralla died in the confrontation, and Vitalis was left alone in charge of the covenant.

Vitalis had to prove his loyalty to Salionca, so he was made to sail to the northern Cantabrian Sea with the aim of defeating the sirens that dwelt in those waters and so winning the vis sources they guarded. Vitalis, however, failed to strike any agreement; he returned to Izaro by magic and abandoned the entire crew of the ship to its fate. His actions were condemned by Salionca, and Vitalis was expelled from Izaro in 982. By then the covenant's autocrat already had the knowledge and magic items needed to exploit the coastal vis sources and controlled all the mundane trade passing through its port, so Salionca decided to close the covenant and abandon it.

> #### Story Seeds: The Serenas of Izaro
>
> When, in 1147, the crusader Osborne reached the fortified island of Cimavilla after setting sail from the English town of Dartmouth bound for Damascus, he described the song of the serenas as "a lament of pain that turns into laughter."[^p159-VIII] And it is no wonder that he heard them: the Cantabrian Sea is full of them.
>
> Since Izaro's failed attempt to rule the waters of the Cantabrian Sea, no one has ventured again into the sirens' domains. Although Aedes Saturni's cartographic records show an area north of Izaro marked as a possible vis source, no covenant has thought it worth claiming. Most magi consider them poor sources, though in truth no one has verified them *in situ*.
>
> This vis source is a good opportunity for the player characters to venture into the Cantabrian Sea and explore its waters. They are sure to run into serenas, but the reward will be worth it — won't it?
>
> [^p159-VIII]: Taken from Álvarez Peña, 2001.

> #### The Serenas of the Cantabrian Sea
>
> The serenas' statistics have been built following the guidelines and rules of the *Realms of Power: Magic* supplement, although they can be used without that book.
>

>**Virtues and Flaws:** Magic Human; Magical Monster; Ways of the Ocean; Improved Characteristics, Tough (fish scales), Inoffensive to Animals, Voice of the Ocean (can speak with any ocean animal); Anchored to the Ocean, Baneful Circumstances (when on land), Fragile Constitution, Warped Senses (sensitivity to dryness)<br>
>**Magic Qualities and Inferiorities:** Greater Power, Ritual Power x2; Improved Powers x3; Monstrous Appearance.<br>
>**Personality Traits:** Fishlike +3<br>

>**Appearance:** Like other sirens, the serenas of the Cantabrian Sea have the (scaly) torso of a woman and, instead of legs, a long fish's tail. Their hair ranges from navy blue to bright green, and when they are underwater it floats around their heads like a halo of seaweed.
>
> Serenas are carnivorous and, although they can subsist on the fish of the ocean, they crave human flesh, so they seize the slightest opportunity to capsize any vessel that crosses their domains. They never feed on the flesh of dolphins, however, which they use to obtain information from other parts of the ocean (you can find statistics for dolphins on page 82 of *Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults*). Although they rarely do so, being highly territorial creatures, serenas can swim up rivers and live in lagoons or freshwater springs.
>
> When the first news of them reached the Cantabrian coasts, the Church hastened to condemn them and brand them lustful succubi, which is utterly false, not only because they do not belong to the Infernal Realm but because their essential nature has nothing to do with lust or with the sins that men attribute to them.

#### Setting and Physical Description

The ruins of Izaro stand on a small, elongated island some five hundred meters long and nearly one hundred and fifty meters across at its widest point. The island has hardly any vegetation and is ringed by sea cliffs, which makes it difficult to reach on days of heavy seas. Izaro lies a kilometer and a half from the nearest point of the coast and on sunny days is clearly visible from the mainland. In 1220 nothing remains of Izaro but ruins.

<!-- p. 161 -->

The covenant of Izaro has been plundered many times since Salionca decided to abandon it. The island was not emptied of people immediately, however, but gradually. Its last inhabitants did not leave until the end of the tenth century, when the few remaining families (descendants of Izaro's former inhabitants) were massacred by the *vikingr* (see page 286). Since then, some magi have scoured it in search of magical remains, and Spring magi have even tried to settle it, but Salionca has always managed to make them leave, as it does not want any covenant so close to one of its sources of income.

In 1112, the Flambeau of Salionca held one of the House's gatherings at Izaro, and the apprentices had to manage as best they could to get there in the depths of autumn (indeed, one vanished during the crossing, and many blamed his loss on the serenas of the Cantabrian Sea).

## The Extremadura

The territorial unit of the Extremadura covers the Duero basin within the kingdom of Castile (its upper reaches and source), and for many years it was the frontier between the Christian and Muslim kingdoms of the Peninsula. Indeed, frontier warfare allowed covenants to be created without oversight from the mundanes,[^p161-16] as was the case with Durato. In the Castilian Extremadura, town councils (*concejos*) such as those of Soria, Sepúlveda, Valladolid, Peñafiel and Tordesillas, among others, are flourishing.

The Castilian Extremadura has not been an attractive place for Hermetic magi, as it was frontier land for years and was always exposed to pillage and plunder. That is why the only covenant found there is Durato, established after the definitive Christian conquest.

[^p161-16]: This privilege ended, however, in 1076, the year the fuero of Sepúlveda was granted, which required every community to be bound to a jurisdiction of higher rank.

### Durato

>**Lifespan:** 1018–Present<br>
>**Founders:** Domingo Garcés Trianomae, Maʿbad al-Ŷerbitonī, Al-Garīd al-Ŷerbitonī<br>
>**Season:** Summer<br>
>**Aura (type and strength):** Divine, strength 3<br>
>**Reputations:** Even-Handed (Iberian Tribunal) 6, Pious (Iberian Tribunal) 3<br>
>**Votes:** 5

Durato lies deep in the gorges of the Duratón river and was founded by three survivors of the Schism War. The magi built the covenant a few years after the count of Castile, Sancho García, definitively conquered Sepúlveda in 1010, and they chose the site even though they knew there were numerous hermitages carved into the rock in the surrounding area (created in the sixth century following the conversion of the Visigothic king Reccared to Christianity). In 1220 hermits still occupy many of the caves of the Duratón.

#### History

When the Trianomae Ḥafṣa ibn ʿAbbās al-Bonisagiyya of Dār Malīḥaʾ called on the Tribunal not to take part in the Schism War, her former apprentice, Domingo Garcés, and two of the covenant's most eminent members, the musicians and poets Maʿbad and Al-Garīd al-Ŷerbitonī, left the covenant and went off to fight the Diedne of the Peninsula. The three traveled to the Stonehenge Tribunal and stayed there until the end of the war alongside Brutus. Afterward they returned to their home Tribunal to settle in a covenant they named Durato.

The three magi took advantage of the resettlement of the area promoted by the Leonese monarch Alfonso V after the restoration of important military strongholds such as Curiel and Peñafiel. As the first magi to occupy the region, they were able to claim the vis sources of the surrounding area. However, although they had chosen an area untouched by Hermetic magic, it was not yet pacified; the many Muslim raids (*algaras*) that reached their lands forced them to seek a better-protected site. So, a few years before Alfonso VI conquered Toledo, the three magi moved to the floor of the river canyon, where they built an impressive magical fortress wholly sheltered from prying eyes.

After the conquest of Toledo and the improved defenses of the passes through the central mountains, the magi of Durato began to enjoy periods free of Muslim incursions into their lands. They then began to experience a certain magical and mundane prosperity. Durato specialized in raising sheep and introduced its wool into the English and Flemish markets.

Durato was one of those chiefly responsible for holding the Tribunal together during the period known as "The Disintegration of the Iberian Tribunal." Domingo Garcés al-Trianomī, former apprentice of Ḥafṣa ibn ʿAbbās (the first Praeco of al-Andalus), attained the title of Autumn Tenens (see *Houses of Hermes: True Lineages*, page 13) and acted as mediator throughout the disintegration and at the decisive Tribunal of al-Andalus of 1089, working with the judges of Duresca and the Praecones of both Tribunals. Thanks to Durato, the Tribunal succeeded in having al-Andalus rejoin Iberia peacefully in 1103. In recognition of its work, Durato was rewarded with the title of dedicated covenant, and ever since it has continued to watch over the unity and stability of the Tribunal, always in collaboration with other covenants or groups of magi, such as Duresca, Dār Malīḥaʾ, the Mercer Houses and the Praecones.

At present Durato is focused on averting the Almohad threat, and it has become involved in mundane affairs to such an extent that, were it any other covenant, it would already have been expelled from the Order. In addition to the influence it wields in North Africa, in 1216, with the help of Dār Malīḥaʾ, it induced a group of important ulema in Seville to launch their campaign to discredit the Almohad rulers, so the maga Nazhūn believes the end of their dominion in the Peninsula is near.

<!-- p. 162 -->

#### Setting and Physical Description

The impressive covenant of Durato is set deep in the canyon of the Duratón river, inside a sharp meander. Built as a fortress without towers, Durato's walls rise straight out of the water and have no windows. The covenant also has several posts carved into the canyon walls to watch the course of the river, both upstream and downstream. Whatever approaches along the river, Durato knows of it five Diameters before it reaches its gates. Durato also controls a landing stage on each bank, which it uses to bring in supplies and to allow Redcaps and other visitors to reach the covenant.

The body of Durato's fortress is entirely solid, save for a small cloister built in the mid-twelfth century. Although the magi knew they were weakening the structure, they decided to build it so as to have a space in which to stroll and look up at the sky. Otherwise, everything in Durato is practical to the point of austerity: its *sancta*, its council chamber, its spacious reading rooms, even its magi… the covenant lacks ornamental luxuries and even windows. The only distraction allowed them is reading the hundreds of books they jealously guard in its vaulted cellars — a pastime that has grown since a Divine aura arose in the covenant (see the insert on the next page), as the magi prefer not to spend too much time experimenting in their laboratories.

#### Society and Customs

Since its founding in 1018, Durato has functioned as a democracy. All its members call themselves *fratres* ("brothers" in Latin; *frater* in the singular) or *sorores* ("sisters"; *soror* in the singular), and each has one vote (even without a voting sigil) with which to take part in the covenant's councils. All members of Durato have access to the same resources, regardless of office or age. Its charter grants no privilege to any magus or House above the others, and to join the covenant one must renounce private property and learn to lead a humble life free of sin (almost all its members have the Minor Personality Flaw Vow); its members must also swear to devote their lives to the Tribunal, so they are obliged to help the Trianomae of the Order (whether members of the covenant or not) whenever these require it. Any member who, having sworn the covenant's charter, fails to observe these simple rules will be brought before the Iberian Tribunal for having committed a low crime, which usually entails performing one or more tasks for Durato followed by expulsion from the Tribunal.

Durato's charter stipulates that none of its members may seek election as Praeco and, should one be elected nonetheless, he must withdraw his candidacy whenever possible. Furthermore, out of deference to its founders, the language spoken at Durato is Arabic.

Throughout its existence, Durato has worked shoulder to shoulder with the Quaesitores of the Tribunal and has always preferred the magi of the Ronda covenant of Dār Malīḥaʾ to the judges of Duresca.

#### The Magi of Durato

##### Soror Nazhūn bint Domingo al-Trianomiyya

The maga Nazhūn, a native of Granada, was apprenticed to Domingo Garcés, so she learned the secrets of the craft by watching her master at work. Through his influence she was named Spring Tenens after passing her House's Gauntlet, and she now carries out the difficult task of neutralizing the Almohad threat and halting the exodus from Iberia, always with the help of the members of the Iberian Chamber, with whom she meets every ten years. Nazhūn must also deal with the other conflicts that arise across the Iberian lands, such as keeping what is happening at Duresca from coming to light, watching the movements of the covenant of ʾAlif, and coping with the constant violations committed by the Andalusi covenant of Chazāʾir, among other things.

<!-- p. 163 -->

Nazhūn always travels with her apprentice, the still-child Saʿīd al-Tulaytulī, and with her *amicus*, the *frater* ʿUsfūr-al-Šawk al-Biŷornī, who is so useful to her in learning everything the winds of Iberia carry. Depending on the nature of her journeys, she may also be accompanied by the *fratres* Muʿāwiya or Vitiza, or by the archmage Danāʾ.

##### Frater ʿUsfūr-al-Šawk al-Biŷornī

The Bjornaer magus ʿUsfūr-al-Šawk (a *laqab* meaning "little bird in the shelter of the thorns") is the *amicus* of the Trianomae Nazhūn and always accompanies her on her journeys and negotiations (in the latter case never in human form). When he is not traveling the Tribunal, his *fratres* and *sorores* enjoy his melodious song, for few sounds ever break the heavy silence of Durato.

ʿUsfūr-al-Šawk is a very old magus whose heartbeast is a small starling. Thanks to his abilities, he can ride the wind and gather the information it carries, so Nazhūn has more than once made use of his services to stay one step ahead of events.

##### Frater Vitiza al-Gernikī

Vitiza is the covenant's only Guernicus. He was trained at Dār Malīḥaʾ and, like his predecessor, sent to Durato to assist the Trianomae. Vitiza deals mainly with the covenant's legal affairs; he could be described as its legal counsel. Among his other duties, he has also been entrusted with the task of dispelling the Divine aura that has engulfed the covenant, although he barely has time for it and is thinking of delegating this responsibility. Indeed, the burden of the Divine aura has been vexing the inhabitants of Durato for decades and is to blame for the prolongation of its already long Summer.

> #### Story Seeds: The Divine Aura of Durato
>
> When Maʿbad, Al-Garīd and Domingo Garcés moved to the floor of the Duratón gorge, there was a by no means negligible Magic aura of strength 5 (despite the many hermitages in the area). In the autumn of 1111, however, the aura changed: the Magic aura vanished and in its place a Divine aura of strength 3 sprang up. As a result, some of the *fratres* present at Durato underwent Twilight (the then very young ʿUsfūr-al-Šawk was especially affected), and they blamed the change on the consecration of the newly built hermitage of Frutos, barely three bends of the meander upstream from the covenant, where a miracle had taken place in the eighth century.
>
> In an attempt to weaken the Divine aura, the magi of Durato cleared several nearby hermitages in the mid-twelfth century. But the Divine aura was unaffected. Now that *frater* Vitiza is in charge of the problem, he has proposed expelling the abbot of the hermitage of Frutos and driving off the monks who accompany him, but neither *soror* Nazhūn nor the others agree, so the only alternative he can think of is to move. For now, however, no one even wants to think about it, so he has asked Muʿāwiya to look for ideas and possible candidates to solve the problem among the covenants he visits. In exchange, Durato will hand over a vis source and allow several of the covenant's books to be copied by whoever solves this problem. Will the player characters' magi want to take on the task?

##### Frater Muʿāwiya al-Merkerī

Muʿāwiya is Durato's resident Redcap. A native of al-Gharb, he was trained at Porta Pandere and sent to the covenant barely seven years ago. His youth does not interfere with his work, however, of which the other *fratres* and *sorores* are very proud. As a member of Durato he has access to all manner of enchanted items, so although he lacks the Gift, he is far from defenseless.

*Frater* Muʿāwiya helps the Trianomae Nazhūn in many ways, whether by acting as a guide, organizing Durato's mundane agents, gathering information from the covenants he visits, spreading rumors or refuting them, or changing the minds of those who listen to him (Muʿāwiya is a great orator with a natural talent for steering arguments onto his own ground). He is also an excellent chess player, and on more than one occasion he has settled a dispute in his favor over the board. The only problem he has not yet been able to solve is that of the Verditius agents of Ajabeba. When they cross paths with Durato's network of agents, one of its members usually ends up dead. For that reason, whenever he identifies a Verditius agent, he takes extreme precautions.

##### Soror Danāʾ al-Qurtubiyya al-Ŷerbitoniyya

*Soror* Danāʾ al-Ŷerbitoniyya is an excellent warrior. A native of the city of Cordoba, the archmage and hoplite Danāʾ is in charge of the defense of Durato and, ultimately, of the Tribunal. Together with Muchāhid al-Muwaffaq al-Ŷerbitonī, Danāʾ is responsible for protecting the covenant from any outside influence or attack, so one or the other must be present at all times. Her reputation is such that the mere mention of her name is defense enough to prevent any member of Durato from being attacked by another magus of the Tribunal. Naturally, when *soror* Nazhūn requires it, Danāʾ places herself at her service, which usually smooths things over considerably.

##### Frater Muchāhid al-Muwaffaq al-Ŷerbitonī

The young Muchāhid was Danāʾ's apprentice and, like his *parens*, he is charged with protecting the *fratres* and *sorores* of the covenant and Durato itself. Although he is still very young, he enjoys the protection afforded by the reputation of both Durato and his mistress. In any case, anyone wishing to attack the covenant had better hope that Muchāhid, and not Danāʾ, is the one on guard.

<!-- p. 164 -->

## The Transierra

The territorial unit of the Transierra covers the central mountain range of the Peninsula. Among its mountains rises the highest peak in the whole kingdom, the Almanzor (named, it is said, in honor of the *ḥaŷib* Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAmir, the first man to reach its summit), and numerous vis sources abound there, most of them claimed by the Toledan covenant of Iššáh.

After Alfonso VI's conquest of Toledo in 1085, the Transierra ceased to be a battleground between Cordoba and the Christian kings, and in 1220 it is home to the important town councils (*concejos*) of Ávila, Alcalá, Madrid and Guadalajara, among others. At present the region has no living covenant, although the mountains were once ruled by the magi of the Diedne covenant of Nebula.

### Nebula

>**Lifespan:** 871–1017<br>
>**Founders:** Efrddyl of Diedne, Gwladus of Diedne<br>
>**Aura (type and strength):** Magic, strength 7 (Peñalara)<br>
>**Reputations:** None

In 1025 the Iberian Tribunal passed the Peripheral Code ruling "On the Diedne Legacy," under which all records relating to that House were destroyed. So although both its location and its history are described here, all this knowledge was lost, and should Duresca have kept a copy of all its records, that information would be reserved for a few magi of the Tribunal.

#### History

The magi Efrddyl and Gwladus were trained at Duresca, where they lived their first years after passing their Gauntlet and from which they departed in 845, after the monarch of Asturias, Ramiro I, condemned all the wizards of his kingdom to the pyre. Drawn by the immense power emanating from the central mountain range, the Diedne pair explored its mountains for several decades and, having traveled its valleys, slopes, peaks and lakes, settled there, making their main building the one they raised in the shadow of Peñalara, beside the great lake of wintry waters that the magi of Mons Vindius said was a node of communication with other bodies of water. Its founding coincided with that of the Diedne covenant of Ipagrum in al-Andalus, which was also built beside one of these lakes.

Efrddyl and Gwladus built another of Nebula's buildings beside the great lake of Gredos, in the shadow of the peak that would come to be called Almanzor, and raised numerous stone circles at many of the lakes of the range, which they used to perform their rites or to mark ancient places of power of the gods they worshipped.

Nebula took little part in politics during its lifetime. Its name only began to be known when the Schism War broke out, for it helped destroy Tremébriga and took part in the failed attacks against Duresca, Tertia and Salionca. Nebula was the last Diedne covenant of the Tribunal to fall during the war. In the first days of winter of 1017, the forces of the Order, led by the hero and archmage Brutus of Flambeau, razed all its buildings and evaporated its lakes to prevent any other Diedne from escaping through them (see *Realms of Power: Magic*, page 137).

#### Setting and Physical Description

The ruins of Nebula are scattered throughout the central mountain range, almost always beside large lakes, although in 1220 they are hard to locate: what remained after the Schism War was razed following the decree of 1025. At best it may be possible to make out some remnant of stone whose cut or composition betrays its connection with the Diedne (like Mons Vindius, Nebula was built with stones brought from Asturias, Galicia and Wales).

> #### Story Seeds: The Legacy of Nebula
>
> ##### Seeking a Home in Gredos
>
> The player characters' magi are looking for a place to live and decide to settle in the Sierra de Gredos so as to have no contact with the mundane powers. During the first winter they spend at the covenant, however, they receive a visit from a strange woman, who arrives at night and asks them for shelter. Although she looks like a peasant, she is in fact a lake woman, of the lineage that helped the Diedne during the Schism War. Perhaps she has come to observe the magi and gather information, or perhaps she still remembers how the magi of the Order destroyed her people's homes during the war. What has prompted her visit? What will the characters do to find out?
>
> ##### The Disappearance of the Redcaps
>
> At the next ordinary Tribunal (for example, that of 1221), the representative of Aedes Saturni recounts the disappearance of several Redcaps who were mapping the Sierra de Gredos. Anyone who succeeds at an Iberian Tribunal Lore roll of 6+ recalls the uncensored events of the Schism War and remembers how that whole area was once controlled by the Diedne. In exchange for a pawn or two of vis or a book (at the storyguide's discretion), the Tribunal asks for volunteers to investigate the mountains and find the missing Redcaps. If the player characters accept, what will they find in the mountains?
